bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第168卷卷第一百六十八

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 168, Roll 168
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 168

sentences.zh: 【陳紀二】　起上章執徐，盡玄黓敦牂，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Chen Records 2] From Shangzhang Zhixu through Xuanyi Dunzang; three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Chen Records 2] From Shangzhang Zhixu through Xuanyi Dunzang—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸丑朔，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the guichou new moon, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the guichou new moon, Chen Qian proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 齊大赦，改元乾明。

translations.literal: Qi proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Qianming.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Qianming.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Chen Qian sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 齊高陽王湜，以滑稽便辟有寵於顯祖，常在左右，執杖以撻諸王，太皇太后深銜之。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's Prince Gao of Gaoyang, Shi, by buffoonery and ready flattery won favor with Emperor Xianzu, was constantly at his side, and wielded a staff to thrash the princes; the empress dowager deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Prince Gao of Gaoyang, Gao Shi, by buffoonery and ready flattery won favor with Gao Yang, was constantly at his side, and wielded a staff to thrash the princes; the empress dowager deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 及顯祖殂，湜有罪，太皇太后杖之百餘；

translations.literal: When Xianzu died, Shi had guilt upon him; the empress dowager had him beaten more than a hundred strokes;
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yang died, Shi was found guilty; the empress dowager had him beaten more than a hundred strokes;

sentences.zh: 癸亥，卒。

translations.literal: on guihai he died.
translations.idiomatic: on guihai he died.

sentences.zh: 辛未，上祀北郊。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the emperor sacrificed at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Chen Qian sacrificed at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 齊主自晉陽還至鄴。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler returned from Jinyang to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi ruler returned from Jinyang to Ye.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙未，高州刺史紀機自軍所逃還宣城，據郡應王琳，涇令賀當遷討平之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yiwei, Gaozhou Inspector Ji Ji fled from the army back to Xuancheng, seized the commandery to join Wang Lin, and Jing Magistrate He Dangqian campaigned and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yiwei, Gaozhou inspector Ji Ji fled from the army back to Xuancheng, seized the commandery to join Wang Lin, and Jing magistrate He Dangqian campaigned and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 王琳至柵口，侯瑱督諸軍出屯蕪湖，相持百餘日。

translations.literal: Wang Lin reached Zhakou; Hou Tian supervised the armies and marched out to encamp at Wuhu; they faced each other for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin reached Zhakou; Hou Tian supervised the armies and marched out to encamp at Wuhu; the two sides faced each other for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 東關春水稍長，舟艦得通，琳引合肥漅湖之眾，舳艫相次而下，軍勢甚盛。

translations.literal: The spring waters at Dongguan rose somewhat; boats and ships could pass; Lin led the masses from Hefei and Chaohu; war vessels followed one after another downstream; his army's momentum was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: The spring waters at Dongguan rose; boats could pass; Wang Lin led the forces from Hefei and Chaohu downstream in a long column of war vessels; his army's momentum was formidable.

sentences.zh: 瑱進軍虎檻洲，琳亦出船列於江西，隔洲而泊。

translations.literal: Tian advanced to Tiger Cage Ford; Lin also sent out ships arrayed on the west of the river and moored across the ford from him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tian advanced to Tiger Cage Ford; Wang Lin also sent out ships on the west bank and moored across the ford from him.

sentences.zh: 明日，合戰，琳軍少卻，退保西岸。

translations.literal: The next day they joined battle; Lin's army fell back slightly and withdrew to hold the west bank.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they joined battle; Wang Lin's army fell back slightly and withdrew to hold the west bank.

sentences.zh: 及夕，東北風大起，吹其舟艦並壞，沒於沙中。

translations.literal: By evening a great northeast wind rose, blew his boats and ships to ruin, and they sank in the sand.
translations.idiomatic: By evening a great northeast wind rose, wrecked his fleet, and drove the ships into the sand.

sentences.zh: 浪大，不得還浦。

translations.literal: The waves were high and he could not return to the harbor.
translations.idiomatic: The waves were too high to return to harbor.

sentences.zh: 及旦，風靜，琳入浦治船，瑱等亦引軍退入蕪湖。

translations.literal: At dawn the wind stilled; Lin entered the harbor to repair ships; Tian and the rest also withdrew the army into Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the wind stilled; Wang Lin entered the harbor to repair his ships; Hou Tian and the rest withdrew into Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 周人聞琳東下，遣都督荊、襄等五十二州諸軍事、荊州刺史史寧將兵數萬乘虛襲郢州，孫瑒嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Zhou men heard Lin was heading east and sent Area Commander of military affairs for fifty-two provinces including Jing and Xiang, Jingzhou Inspector Shi Ning, to lead tens of thousands of troops and strike Yingzhou while it was empty; Sun Yong closed the walls and defended himself.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou heard Wang Lin was heading east and sent area commander of military affairs for fifty-two provinces including Jing and Xiang, Jingzhou inspector Shi Ning, with tens of thousands of troops to strike Yingzhou while it was empty; Sun Yong closed the walls and defended himself.

sentences.zh: 琳聞之，恐其眾潰，乃帥舟師東下，去蕪湖十里而泊，擊柝聞於陳軍。

translations.literal: Lin heard this, feared his masses would scatter, and thereupon led the fleet east; he moored ten li from Wuhu, and the night-watch clappers were heard in the Chen army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin heard this, feared his troops would scatter, led the fleet east, moored ten li from Wuhu, and the night-watch clappers were heard in the Chen camp.

sentences.zh: 齊儀同三司劉伯球將兵萬餘人助琳水戰，行台慕容恃德之子子會將鐵騎二千，屯蕪湖西岸，為之聲勢。

translations.literal: Qi's Acting Three Excellencies Liu Boqiu led more than ten thousand men to aid Lin in the water battle; Mobile Headquarters Murong Shide's son Zihui led two thousand iron cavalry, encamped on Wuhu's west bank, and lent him momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Liu Boqiu, equal in honor to the three dukes, led more than ten thousand men to aid Wang Lin on the water; Murong Shide's son Zihui led two thousand iron cavalry on Wuhu's west bank to lend him momentum.

sentences.zh: 丙申，瑱令軍中晨炊蓐食以待之。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Tian ordered the army to cook in the morning and take bedding rations in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Hou Tian ordered the army to cook at dawn and eat from their bedding in readiness.

sentences.zh: 時西南風急，琳自謂得天助，引兵直趣建康。

translations.literal: At the time the southwest wind was fierce; Lin thought Heaven was helping him and led his troops straight for Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The southwest wind was fierce; Wang Lin thought Heaven was helping him and led his troops straight for Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 瑱等徐出蕪湖躡其後，西南風翻為瑱用。

translations.literal: Tian and the rest slowly came out of Wuhu and followed on his heels; the southwest wind turned to Tian's use.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tian and the rest slowly came out of Wuhu and followed on his heels; the southwest wind turned in Hou Tian's favor.

sentences.zh: 琳擲火炬以燒陳船，皆反燒其船。

translations.literal: Lin threw torches to burn Chen ships; all turned back and burned his own ships.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin threw torches to burn Chen ships; the flames turned back and burned his own fleet.

sentences.zh: 瑱發拍以擊琳艦，又以牛皮冒蒙沖小船以觸其艦，並熔鐵灑之。

translations.literal: Tian loosed catapults to strike Lin's war vessels, also covered assault boats in oxhide to ram his ships, and poured molten iron as well.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tian loosed catapults against Wang Lin's ships, covered assault boats in oxhide to ram them, and poured molten iron as well.

sentences.zh: 琳軍大敗，軍士溺死者什二三，餘皆棄船登岸走，為陳軍所殺殆盡。

translations.literal: Lin's army was greatly defeated; two or three tenths of the soldiers drowned; the rest all abandoned their ships, fled ashore, and were nearly all killed by the Chen army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin's army was routed; two or three tenths of his men drowned; the rest abandoned their ships and fled ashore, where the Chen army killed nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 齊步騎在西岸者，自相蹂踐，並陷於蘆荻泥淖中；

translations.literal: Qi's foot and horse on the west bank trampled one another and all sank into reed marsh and mud;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's foot and horse on the west bank trampled one another and sank into the reed marsh and mud;

sentences.zh: 騎皆棄馬脫走，得免者什二三。

translations.literal: the horsemen all abandoned their horses and fled on foot; two or three tenths escaped.
translations.idiomatic: the horsemen abandoned their horses and fled on foot; only two or three tenths escaped.

sentences.zh: 擒劉伯球、慕容子會，斬獲萬計，盡收梁、齊軍資器械。

translations.literal: Liu Boqiu and Murong Zihui were captured; beheaded and seized were counted by the myriad; all Liang and Qi military stores and weapons were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Boqiu and Murong Zihui were captured; the dead and captured numbered in the tens of thousands; all Liang and Northern Qi stores and weapons were seized.

sentences.zh: 琳乘舴艋冒陳走，至湓城，欲收合離散，眾無附者，乃與妻妾左右十餘人奔齊。

translations.literal: Lin took a skiff and broke through the Chen lines, fled to Pencheng, wished to gather the scattered, but none would join him; he then fled to Qi with his wife, concubines, and a dozen attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin took a skiff and broke through the Chen lines, fled to Pencheng, tried to rally the scattered, but none would follow; he fled to Northern Qi with his wife, concubines, and a dozen attendants.

sentences.zh: 先是，琳使侍中袁泌、御史中丞劉仲威侍衛永嘉王莊；

translations.literal: Earlier, Lin had sent Palace Attendant Yuan Bi and Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhongwei to attend Prince Zhuang of Yongjia;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Lin had sent palace attendant Yuan Bi and censor-in-chief Liu Zhongwei to attend Prince Zhuang of Yongjia;

sentences.zh: 及敗，左右皆散。

translations.literal: when he was defeated, his attendants all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: when he was defeated, his attendants all scattered.

sentences.zh: 泌以輕舟送莊達於齊境，拜辭而還，遂來降；

translations.literal: Bi with a light boat sent Zhuang to the Qi border, bowed in farewell and returned, and thereupon came to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Bi sent Zhuang to the Qi border in a light boat, bowed in farewell and returned, and surrendered to Chen;

sentences.zh: 仲威奉莊奔齊。

translations.literal: Zhongwei escorted Zhuang and fled to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongwei escorted Zhuang and fled to Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 泌，昂之子也。

translations.literal: Bi was the son of Ang.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was the son of Yuan Ang.

sentences.zh: 樊猛及其兄毅帥部曲來降。

translations.literal: Fan Meng and his elder brother Yi led their household troops to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Meng and his elder brother Yi led their household troops to surrender.

sentences.zh: 齊葬文宣皇帝於武寧陵，廟號高祖，後改曰顯祖。

translations.literal: Qi buried Emperor Wenxuan at Wuning Mausoleum; his temple name was Gaozu, later changed to Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi buried Gao Yang at Wuning Mausoleum; his temple name was Gaozu, later changed to Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，詔：「衣冠士族、將帥戰兵陷在王琳黨中者，皆赦之，隨材銓敘。

translations.literal: On wuxu, an edict said, "Gentry and clansmen, generals, and fighting soldiers trapped in Wang Lin's faction are all pardoned and will be appointed according to their talents.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, an edict said, "Gentry, generals, and soldiers trapped in Wang Lin's faction are all pardoned and will be appointed according to their talents.

sentences.zh: 己亥，齊以常山王演為太師、錄尚書事，以長廣王湛為大司馬、並省錄尚書事，以尚書左僕射平秦王歸彥為司空，趙郡王睿為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On jihai, Qi made Prince Yan of Changshan Grand Preceptor and recorder of the masters of writing, Prince Zhan of Changgung Grand Marshal and recorder for the merged provinces, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Prince Guiyan of Pingqin Minister of Works, and Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Northern Qi made Prince Yan of Changshan grand preceptor and recorder of the masters of writing, Prince Zhan of Changgung grand marshal and recorder for the merged provinces, left vice director Prince Guiyan of Pingqin minister of works, and Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery left vice director.

sentences.zh: 詔：「諸元良口配沒入官及賜人者並縱遣。

translations.literal: An edict said, "All good people of Yuan descent assigned to government service or given to others are all released.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "All good people of Northern Wei Yuan descent assigned to government service or given to others are all released.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以太尉侯瑱都督湘、巴等五州諸軍事，鎮湓城。

translations.literal: On yisi, Grand Commandant Hou Tian was made area commander of military affairs for five provinces including Xiang and Ba, and garrisoned Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, grand commandant Hou Tian was made area commander of military affairs for five provinces including Xiang and Ba, and garrisoned Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 齊顯祖之喪，常山王演居禁中護喪事，婁太后欲立之而不果；

translations.literal: At Northern Qi Emperor Xianzu's funeral, Prince Yan of Changshan dwelt in the forbidden quarters to oversee mourning; Empress Dowager Lou wished to install him but did not succeed;
translations.idiomatic: At Gao Yang's funeral, Prince Yan of Changshan dwelt in the forbidden quarters to oversee mourning; Empress Dowager Lou wished to install him but did not succeed;

sentences.zh: 太子即位，乃就朝列。

translations.literal: the crown prince took the throne and he then took his place in court.
translations.idiomatic: the crown prince took the throne and he then took his place at court.

sentences.zh: 以天子諒陰，詔演居東館，欲奏之事，皆先咨決。

translations.literal: Because the Son of Heaven was in mourning seclusion, an edict had Yan dwell in the Eastern Lodge; matters to be memorialized were all first consulted and decided with him.
translations.idiomatic: Because the new emperor was in mourning seclusion, an edict had Gao Yan dwell in the Eastern Lodge; all memorials were first referred to him for decision.

sentences.zh: 楊愔等以演與長廣王湛位地親逼，恐不利於嗣主，心忌之。

translations.literal: Yang Yin and the rest, because Yan and Prince Zhan of Changgung were close in rank and position, feared harm to the heir and resented them in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin and the rest, because Gao Yan and Prince Zhan of Changgung were close in rank and power, feared harm to the young emperor and resented them.

sentences.zh: 居頃之，演出歸第，自是詔敕多不關預。

translations.literal: After a short while Yan left and returned to his mansion; from then on edicts and orders mostly did not involve him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gao Yan left the palace for his mansion; from then on edicts and orders mostly bypassed him.

sentences.zh: 或謂演曰：「鷙鳥離巢，必有探卵之患。

translations.literal: Someone said to Yan, "When a fierce bird leaves the nest, there is sure to be the harm of one who comes to steal the eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Gao Yan, "When a fierce bird leaves the nest, someone will surely come for the eggs.

sentences.zh: 今日王何宜屢出？

translations.literal: Today, Prince, why should you go out so often?
translations.idiomatic: Prince, why should you go out so often today?

sentences.zh: 」中山太守陽休之詣演，演不見。

translations.literal: " Zhongshan Administrator Yang Xiuzhi called on Yan; Yan would not see him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongshan administrator Yang Xiuzhi called on Gao Yan; Gao Yan would not see him.

sentences.zh: 休之謂王友王晞曰：「昔周公朝讀百篇書，夕見七十士，猶恐不足。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi said to the prince's friend Wang Xi, "In olden days the Duke of Zhou read a hundred chapters of books in the morning and received seventy scholars in the evening, yet still feared it was not enough.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi said to the prince's friend Wang Xi, "In olden days the Duke of Zhou read a hundred chapters in the morning and received seventy scholars in the evening, yet still feared it was not enough.

sentences.zh: 錄王何所嫌疑，乃爾拒絕賓客！

translations.literal: What suspicion does the Recorder Prince have, that he thus refuses guests!
translations.idiomatic: What suspicion does the recorder prince have, that he thus refuses his guests!

sentences.zh: 先是，顯祖之世，群臣人不自保。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Xianzu's time, among the hundred officials none could keep himself safe.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Gao Yang's time, no minister could feel safe.

sentences.zh: 及濟南王立，演謂王晞曰：「一人垂拱，吾曹亦保優閒。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jinan was installed, Yan said to Wang Xi, "One man sits with folded hands; we too may keep ease and leisure.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yin was installed, Gao Yan said to Wang Xi, "One man sits with folded hands; we too may keep our ease.

sentences.zh: 」因言：「朝廷寬仁，真守文良主。

translations.literal: " He went on, "The court is lenient and humane—a true heir who keeps the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: " He went on, "The court is lenient and humane—a true heir who keeps the statutes.

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「先帝時，東宮委一胡人傅之。

translations.literal: " Xi said, "In the late emperor's time the Eastern Palace was entrusted to one Hu tutor.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "In the late emperor's time the Eastern Palace was entrusted to one Hu tutor.

sentences.zh: 今春秋尚富，驟覽萬機，殿下宜朝夕先後，親承音旨。

translations.literal: Now his years are still young and he suddenly oversees the myriad affairs; Your Highness ought morning and evening to go before and after, personally receiving his instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor is still young and suddenly oversees all affairs; Your Highness ought morning and evening to attend him personally and receive his instructions.

sentences.zh: 而使他姓出納詔命，大權必有所歸，殿下雖欲守籓，其可得邪！

translations.literal: Yet another surname handles edicts in and out; great power must go somewhere—though Your Highness wishes to keep to your fief, how can you obtain it!
translations.idiomatic: Yet another clan handles the edicts; great power must go somewhere—though Your Highness wishes to keep to your fief, how can you?

sentences.zh: 借令得遂沖退，自審家祚得保靈長乎？

translations.literal: Even if you could achieve modest withdrawal, do you yourself judge that your house's fortune can be kept long and numinous?
translations.idiomatic: Even if you could achieve modest withdrawal, do you judge that your house's fortune can endure?

sentences.zh: 」演默然久之，曰：「何以處我？

translations.literal: " Yan was silent a long while and said, "How am I to be placed?
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Yan was silent a long while and said, "What am I to do?

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「周公抱成王攝政七年，然後復子明辟，惟殿下慮之！

translations.literal: " Xi said, "The Duke of Zhou held King Cheng and governed as regent seven years, then restored the son and clarified the court—only Your Highness must consider it!
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "The Duke of Zhou held King Cheng and governed as regent seven years, then restored the son and clarified the court—only Your Highness must consider it!

sentences.zh: 」演曰：「我何敢自比周公！

translations.literal: " Yan said, "How dare I compare myself to the Duke of Zhou!
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Yan said, "How dare I compare myself to the Duke of Zhou!

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「殿下今日地望，欲不為周公，得邪？

translations.literal: " Xi said, "Your Highness's position and renown today—if you do not wish to be the Duke of Zhou, can you obtain that?
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "With Your Highness's position and renown today—if you do not wish to be the Duke of Zhou, can you avoid it?

sentences.zh: 」演不應。

translations.literal: " Yan did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Yan did not answer.

sentences.zh: 顯祖常使胡人康虎兒保護太子，故晞言及之。

translations.literal: Xianzu had often had the Hu Kang Hu'er protect the crown prince; therefore Xi spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang had often had the Hu Kang Hu'er protect the crown prince; therefore Wang Xi spoke of it.

sentences.zh: 齊主將發晉陽，時議謂常山王必當留守根本之地；

translations.literal: The Qi ruler was about to set out from Jinyang; current opinion held that the Prince of Changshan must surely remain to guard the root lands;
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi ruler was about to set out from Jinyang; opinion held that Prince Yan of Changshan must remain to guard the heartland;

sentences.zh: 執政欲使常山王從帝之鄴，留長廣王鎮晉陽；

translations.literal: those in power wished the Prince of Changshan to follow the emperor to Ye and leave the Prince of Changgung to garrison Jinyang;
translations.idiomatic: those in power wished Gao Yan to follow the emperor to Ye and leave Prince Zhan of Changgung at Jinyang;

sentences.zh: 既而又疑之，乃敕二王俱從至鄴。

translations.literal: then they doubted again and ordered both princes to follow to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: then they doubted again and ordered both princes to follow to Ye.

sentences.zh: 外朝聞之，莫不駭愕。

translations.literal: The outer court heard this and all were appalled.
translations.idiomatic: The outer court heard this and all were appalled.

sentences.zh: 又敕以王晞為并州長史。

translations.literal: An edict also made Wang Xi Changshan chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also made Wang Xi Bingzhou chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 演既行，晞出郊送之。

translations.literal: When Yan had set out, Xi went to the suburbs to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yan had set out, Wang Xi went to the suburbs to see him off.

sentences.zh: 演恐有覘察，命晞還城，執晞手曰：「努力自慎！

translations.literal: Yan feared observers, ordered Xi back to the city, took Xi's hand and said, "Strive and guard yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yan feared observers, ordered Xi back to the city, took his hand and said, "Strive and guard yourself!

sentences.zh: 」因躍馬而出。

translations.literal: " Then he leapt on his horse and rode out.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he leapt on his horse and rode out.

sentences.zh: 平秦王歸彥總知禁衛，楊愔宣敕留從駕五千兵於西中，陰備非常；

translations.literal: Prince Guiyan of Pingqin oversaw the forbidden guard; Yang Yin proclaimed an edict leaving five thousand troops of the imperial escort at the Western Center as a secret guard against the unexpected;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guiyan of Pingqin oversaw the forbidden guard; Yang Yin proclaimed an edict leaving five thousand troops of the imperial escort at the Western Center as a secret guard against the unexpected;

sentences.zh: 至鄴數日，歸彥乃知之，由是怨愔。

translations.literal: after several days at Ye Guiyan learned of it; from this he resented Yin.
translations.idiomatic: after several days at Ye Guiyan learned of it; from this he resented Yang Yin.

sentences.zh: 領軍大將軍可朱渾天和，道元之子也，尚帝姑東平公主，每曰：「若不誅二王，少主無自安之理。

translations.literal: Garrison-general Kezhunhun Tianhe, son of Daoyuan, had married the emperor's aunt Princess Dongping, and often said, "If the two princes are not executed, the young lord has no principle by which to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison-general Kezhunhun Tianhe, son of Daoyuan, had married the emperor's aunt Princess Dongping, and often said, "If the two princes are not executed, the young emperor cannot be secure.

sentences.zh: 」燕子獻謀處太皇太后於北宮，使歸政皇太后。

translations.literal: " Yan Zixian plotted to place the empress dowager in the Northern Palace and restore government to the empress regent.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan Zixian plotted to place the empress dowager in the Northern Palace and restore government to the empress regent.

sentences.zh: 又自天保八年已來，爵賞多濫，楊愔欲加澄汰，乃先自表解開府及開封王，諸叨竊恩榮者皆從黜免。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the eighth year of Tianbao titles and rewards had been excessive; Yang Yin wished to clarify and prune; he first memorialized to resign acting three excellencies and Prince of Kaifeng; all who had stolen favor and glory followed in dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since the eighth year of Tianbao titles and rewards had been excessive; Yang Yin wished to clarify and prune; he first resigned his honors as equal to the three dukes and Prince of Kaifeng; all who had stolen favor followed in dismissal.

sentences.zh: 由是嬖寵失職之徒，盡歸心二叔。

translations.literal: From this those of the emperor's favorites who lost office all gave their hearts to the two uncles.
translations.idiomatic: From this the emperor's favorites who lost office all gave their hearts to the two uncles.

sentences.zh: 平秦王歸彥初與楊、燕同心，既而中變，盡以疏忌之跡告二王。

translations.literal: Prince Guiyan of Pingqin was at first of one mind with Yang and Yan, then turned midway, and reported all signs of estrangement and suspicion to the two princes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guiyan of Pingqin was at first allied with Yang Yin and Yan Zixian, then turned, and reported all signs of estrangement to the two princes.

sentences.zh: 侍中宋欽道，弁之孫也，顯祖使在東宮，教太子以吏事。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Song Qindao, grandson of Bian, Xianzu had placed in the Eastern Palace to teach the crown prince administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Song Qindao, grandson of Song Bian, Gao Yang had placed in the Eastern Palace to teach the crown prince administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 欽道面奏帝，稱「二叔威權既重，宜速去之。

translations.literal: Qindao memorialized the emperor to his face, saying, "The two uncles' authority and power are already heavy—they ought quickly to be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qindao memorialized the emperor to his face, saying, "The two uncles' authority is already heavy—they ought quickly to be removed.

sentences.zh: 」帝不許，曰：「可與令公共詳其事。

translations.literal: " The emperor would not allow it and said, "You may jointly examine the matter with the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused and said, "You may jointly examine the matter with the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 愔等議出二王為刺史，以帝慈仁，恐不可所奏，乃通啟皇太后，具述安危。

translations.literal: Yin and the rest discussed sending the two princes out as inspectors; because the emperor was kind and humane they feared what they memorialized might not be accepted; they therefore sent a joint report to the empress regent, setting forth safety and danger in full.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin and the rest discussed sending the two princes out as inspectors; because the emperor was kind they feared he would refuse; they sent a joint report to the empress regent, setting forth the danger in full.

sentences.zh: 宮人李昌儀，即高仲密之妻也，李太后以其同姓，甚相暱愛，以啟示之；

translations.literal: Palace woman Li Changyi, that is, Gao Zhongmi's wife—Empress Dowager Li, because they shared a surname, was very intimate and fond of her, and showed her the report;
translations.idiomatic: Palace woman Li Changyi, Gao Zhongmi's wife—Empress Dowager Li, because they shared a surname, was very fond of her and showed her the report;

sentences.zh: 昌儀密啟太皇太后。

translations.literal: Changyi secretly reported to the grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changyi secretly reported to the grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 愔等又議不可令二王俱出，乃奏以長廣王湛鎮晉陽，以常山王演錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Yin and the rest again discussed that the two princes must not both be sent out; they memorialized that Prince Zhan of Changgung garrison Jinyang and Prince Yan of Changshan record the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin and the rest again held that both princes must not be sent out; they memorialized that Prince Zhan of Changgung garrison Jinyang and Prince Yan of Changshan record the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 二王既拜職，乙巳，於尚書省大會百僚。

translations.literal: Once the two princes had accepted office, on yisi they held a great assembly of the hundred officials at the Masters of Writing Office.
translations.idiomatic: Once the two princes had accepted office, on yisi they held a great assembly of the hundred officials at the Masters of Writing Office.

sentences.zh: 愔等將赴之，散騎常侍兼中書侍郎鄭頤止之曰：「事未可量，不宜輕脫。

translations.literal: Yin and the rest were about to attend; Regular Attendant and Concurrent Secretariat Gentleman Zheng Yi stopped them, saying, "The affair cannot yet be measured; you ought not go lightly unguarded.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin and the rest were about to attend; regular attendant and concurrent secretariat gentleman Zheng Yi stopped them, saying, "The affair cannot yet be measured; you ought not go unguarded.

sentences.zh: 」愔曰：「吾等至誠體國，豈常山拜職有不赴之理！

translations.literal: " Yin said, "We in utmost sincerity embody the state—when Changshan accepts office is there any principle of not attending!
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Yin said, "We serve the state in utmost sincerity—when Prince Yan of Changshan accepts office how can we not attend!

sentences.zh: 長廣王湛，旦伏家僮數十人於錄尚書後室，仍與席上勳貴賀拔仁、斛律金等數人相知約曰：「行酒至愔等，我各勸雙杯，彼必致辭。

translations.literal: Prince Zhan of Changgung at dawn hid several dozen household slaves in the recorder's rear chamber, and with several nobles at the table such as Heba Ren and Hulu Jin made a mutual pact, saying, "When wine reaches Yin and the rest, each of us will urge a double cup; they are sure to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhan of Changgung at dawn hid several dozen household slaves in the recorder's rear chamber, and with Heba Ren, Hulu Jin, and others at the table made a pact: "When wine reaches Yang Yin and the rest, each of us will urge a double cup; they are sure to decline.

sentences.zh: 我一曰『執酒』，二曰『執酒』，三曰『何不執』，爾輩即執之！

translations.literal: The first time I say 'Hold the wine,' the second 'Hold the wine,' the third 'Why not hold it'—you lot seize them at once!
translations.idiomatic: The first time I say 'Hold the wine,' the second 'Hold the wine,' the third 'Why not hold it'—you seize them at once!

sentences.zh: 」及宴，如之，愔大言曰：「諸王反逆，欲殺忠良邪？

translations.literal: " At the banquet it was so; Yin cried out, "Princes, you rebel—do you wish to kill the loyal and good?
translations.idiomatic: " At the banquet it was so; Yang Yin cried out, "Princes, you rebel—do you mean to kill the loyal?

sentences.zh: 尊天子，削諸侯，赤心奉國，何罪之有！

translations.literal: Honor the Son of Heaven, reduce the feudatories—hearts loyal in serving the state—what crime is there!
translations.idiomatic: Honor the Son of Heaven, reduce the feudatories—hearts loyal in serving the state—what crime is there!

sentences.zh: 」常山王演欲緩之。

translations.literal: " Prince Yan of Changshan wished to ease matters.
translations.idiomatic: " Prince Yan of Changshan wished to ease matters.

sentences.zh: 湛曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Zhan said, "It cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan said, "It cannot be.

sentences.zh: 」於是拳杖亂毆，愔及天和、欽道皆頭面血流，各十人持之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon fists and staves beat them at random; Yin, Tianhe, and Qindao all bled from head and face; ten men each held them.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon fists and staves beat them at random; Yang Yin, Tianhe, and Song Qindao all bled from head and face; ten men each held them.

sentences.zh: 燕子獻多力，頭又少發，狼狽排眾走出門，斛律光逐而擒之。

translations.literal: Yan Zixian was very strong and had little hair on his head; in disarray he pushed through the crowd and ran out the gate; Hulu Guang pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zixian was very strong and nearly bald; in disarray he pushed through the crowd and ran out the gate; Hulu Guang pursued and captured him.

sentences.zh: 子獻歎曰：「丈夫為計遲，遂至於此！

translations.literal: Zixian sighed and said, "A man plans too late and comes to this!
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zixian sighed and said, "A man plans too late and comes to this!

sentences.zh: 」使太子太保薛孤延等執頤於尚藥局。

translations.literal: " He had Crown Prince Guardian Xue Guyuan and the rest seize Yi at the Bureau of Imperial Medicines.
translations.idiomatic: " He had crown prince guardian Xue Guyuan and the rest seize Zheng Yi at the Bureau of Imperial Medicines.

sentences.zh: 頤曰：「不用智者言至此，豈非命也！

translations.literal: Yi said, "By not using the wise man's words we have come to this—is it not fate!
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi said, "By not heeding the wise man's words we have come to this—is it not fate!

sentences.zh: 二王與平秦王歸彥、賀拔仁、斛律金擁愔等唐突入雲龍門，見都督叱利騷，招之，不進，使騎殺之。

translations.literal: The two princes with Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, Heba Ren, and Hulu Jin hustled Yin and the rest in a rush through Cloud Dragon Gate; they saw Commander Chilü Sao, summoned him; he would not advance; they had horsemen kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes with Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, Heba Ren, and Hulu Jin hustled Yang Yin and the rest through Cloud Dragon Gate; they saw commander Chilü Sao, summoned him; he would not advance; they had horsemen kill him.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司成休寧抽刃呵演，演使歸彥諭之，休寧厲聲不從。

translations.literal: Acting Three Excellencies Cheng Xiuning drew his blade and shouted at Yan; Yan had Guiyan instruct him; Xiuning in a harsh voice would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xiuning, equal in honor to the three dukes, drew his blade and shouted at Gao Yan; Gao Yan had Guiyan instruct him; Xiuning in a harsh voice refused.

sentences.zh: 歸彥久為領軍，素為軍士所服，皆弛仗，休寧方歎息而罷。

translations.literal: Guiyan had long been garrison-general and was always obeyed by the soldiers; all laid down their weapons; only then did Xiuning sigh and desist.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan had long been garrison-general and was obeyed by the soldiers; all laid down their weapons; only then did Xiuning sigh and desist.

sentences.zh: 演入，至昭陽殿，湛及歸彥在朱華門外。

translations.literal: Yan entered and reached Zhaoyang Hall; Zhan and Guiyan were outside Vermilion Flower Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yan entered Zhaoyang Hall; Gao Zhan and Guiyan waited outside Vermilion Flower Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝與太皇太后並出，太皇太后坐殿上，皇太后及帝側立。

translations.literal: The emperor and the grand empress dowager came out together; the grand empress dowager sat on the hall; the empress regent and the emperor stood at the side.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and the grand empress dowager came out together; the grand empress dowager sat on the dais; the empress regent and the emperor stood at the side.

sentences.zh: 演以磚叩頭，進言曰：「臣與陛下骨肉至親，楊遵彥等欲獨擅朝權，威福自己，自王公已下皆重足屏氣；

translations.literal: Yan knocked his head with a brick and advanced, saying, "Your servant and Your Majesty are bone and flesh most close; Yang Zunyan and the rest wished to monopolize court power alone, authority and blessing from themselves; from the kings and dukes down all stood on tiptoe and held their breath;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yan knocked his head on the brick floor and said, "Your servant and Your Majesty are closest kin; Yang Zunyan and the rest wished to monopolize court power, making authority and blessing their own; from kings and dukes down all stood in fear;

sentences.zh: 共相脣齒，以成亂階，若不早圖，必為宗社之害。

translations.literal: they were lip and teeth to each other and made the steps of disorder; if not plotted against early, they would surely harm the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: they were lip and teeth to each other and made disorder; if not checked early, they would harm the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 臣與湛為國事重，賀拔仁、斛律金惜獻武皇帝之業，共執遵彥等入宮，未敢刑戮。

translations.literal: Your servant and Zhan took state affairs as weighty; Heba Ren and Hulu Jin cherished Emperor Xianwu's enterprise; together we seized Zunyan and the rest and brought them into the palace; we did not yet dare execution.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant and Zhan took state affairs as weighty; Heba Ren and Hulu Jin cherished Gao Huan's enterprise; together we seized Zunyan and the rest and brought them into the palace; we did not yet dare execute them.

sentences.zh: 專輒之罪，誠當萬死。

translations.literal: The crime of arrogating authority truly deserves ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: The crime of arrogating authority truly deserves death.

sentences.zh: 時庭中及兩廡衛士二千餘人，皆被甲待詔。

translations.literal: At the time in the courtyard and both galleries more than two thousand guards wore armor awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: At the time more than two thousand guards in the courtyard and both galleries wore armor awaiting orders.

sentences.zh: 武衛娥永樂，武力絕倫，素為顯祖所厚，叩刀仰視，帝不睨之。

translations.literal: Martial Guard E Yongle, whose martial strength was unmatched, had always been favored by Xianzu; he struck his blade and looked up; the emperor did not glance at him.
translations.idiomatic: Martial guard E Yongle, whose strength was unmatched, had always been favored by Gao Yang; he struck his blade and looked up; the emperor would not meet his eyes.

sentences.zh: 帝素吃訥，倉猝不知所言。

translations.literal: The emperor had always been halting and slow of speech; in haste he knew not what to say.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had always been halting of speech; in haste he knew not what to say.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后令卻仗，不退；

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager ordered them to lay aside weapons; they did not withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager ordered them to lay aside weapons; they did not withdraw;

sentences.zh: 又厲聲曰：「奴輩即今頭落！

translations.literal: she again said in a harsh voice, "Slaves—your heads fall this instant!
translations.idiomatic: she again said in a harsh voice, "Slaves—your heads fall this instant!

sentences.zh: 」乃退。

translations.literal: " Then they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Then they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 永樂內刀而泣。

translations.literal: Yongle sheathed his blade and wept.
translations.idiomatic: E Yongle sheathed his blade and wept.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后因問：「楊郎何在？

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager thereupon asked, "Where is Master Yang?
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager asked, "Where is Master Yang?

sentences.zh: 」賀拔仁曰：「一眼已出。

translations.literal: " Heba Ren said, "One eye is already out.
translations.idiomatic: " Heba Ren said, "One eye is already out.

sentences.zh: 」太皇太后愴然曰：「楊郎何所能為，留使豈不佳邪！

translations.literal: " The grand empress dowager said mournfully, "What could Master Yang do—would it not have been better to keep him!
translations.idiomatic: " The grand empress dowager said mournfully, "What could Master Yang have done—would it not have been better to keep him!

sentences.zh: 」乃讓帝曰：「此等懷逆，欲殺我二子，次將及我，爾何為縱之！

translations.literal: " She then reproached the emperor, saying, "These men harbored rebellion, wished to kill my two sons, next would reach me—why did you indulge them!
translations.idiomatic: " She then reproached the emperor: "These men harbored rebellion, wished to kill my two sons, next would reach me—why did you indulge them!

sentences.zh: 」帝猶不能言。

translations.literal: " The emperor still could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor still could not speak.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后怒且悲，曰：「豈可使我母子受漢老嫗斟酌！

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager was angry and grieved and said, "How can you let us mother and son be measured out by an old Han crone!
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager was angry and grieved and said, "How can you let us mother and son be ruled by an old Han woman!

sentences.zh: 」太后拜謝。

translations.literal: " The empress regent bowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress regent bowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后又為太后誓言：「演無異志，但欲去逼而已。

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager again swore to the empress regent, "Yan has no other intent—he only wished to remove pressure.
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager again swore to the empress regent, "Gao Yan has no other intent—he only wished to remove pressure.

sentences.zh: 」演叩頭不止。

translations.literal: " Yan knocked his head without cease.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Yan knocked his head without cease.

sentences.zh: 太后謂帝：「何不安慰爾叔！

translations.literal: The empress regent said to the emperor, "Why do you not comfort your uncle!
translations.idiomatic: The empress regent said to the emperor, "Why do you not comfort your uncle!

sentences.zh: 」帝乃曰：「天子亦不敢為叔惜，況此漢輩！

translations.literal: " The emperor then said, "The Son of Heaven dares not spare them for his uncle's sake—how much less these Han fellows!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then said, "The Son of Heaven dares not spare them for his uncle's sake—how much less these Han fellows!

sentences.zh: 但丐兒命，兒自下殿去，此屬任叔父處分。

translations.literal: I only beg my son's life; your son will leave the hall—this lot is left to uncle's disposal.
translations.idiomatic: I only beg my son's life; your son will leave the hall—dispose of this lot as you will.

sentences.zh: 」遂皆斬之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon all were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 長廣王湛以鄭頤昔嘗讒己，先拔其舌，截其手而殺之。

translations.literal: Prince Zhan of Changgung, because Zheng Yi had once slandered him, first pulled out his tongue, cut off his hands, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhan of Changgung, because Zheng Yi had once slandered him, first pulled out his tongue, cut off his hands, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 演令平秦王歸彥引侍衛之士向華林園，以京畿軍士入守門閣，斬娥永樂於園。

translations.literal: Yan ordered Prince Guiyan of Pingqin to lead palace guards toward Hualin Park, bring capital-region soldiers in to guard the gate towers, and behead E Yongle in the park.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yan ordered Prince Guiyan of Pingqin to lead palace guards toward Hualin Park, bring capital-region soldiers to guard the gates, and behead E Yongle in the park.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后臨愔喪，哭曰：「楊郎忠而獲罪。

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager attended Yin's mourning and wept, saying, "Master Yang was loyal yet received punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager attended Yang Yin's mourning and wept, saying, "Master Yang was loyal yet was punished.

sentences.zh: 」以御金為之一眼，親內之，曰：「以表我意。

translations.literal: " She used imperial gold to make one eye, personally placed it within, and said, "To show my mind.
translations.idiomatic: " She used imperial gold to make one eye, placed it in the coffin, and said, "To show my mind.

sentences.zh: 」演亦悔殺之。

translations.literal: " Yan also regretted killing him.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Yan also regretted killing him.

sentences.zh: 於是下詔罪狀愔等，且曰：「罪止一身，家屬不問。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued listing the crimes of Yin and the rest, and said, "Guilt stops at one person; families are not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict listed the crimes of Yang Yin and the rest, and said, "Guilt stops at one person; families are not questioned.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，復簿錄五家；

translations.literal: " Before long, registers were again made of five families;
translations.idiomatic: " Before long, registers were made of five families;

sentences.zh: 王晞固諫，乃各沒一房，孩幼盡死，兄弟皆除名。

translations.literal: Wang Xi firmly remonstrated; thereupon one branch of each was confiscated, infants and young all died, and brothers were all struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi firmly remonstrated; thereupon one branch of each family was confiscated, infants and young were all killed, and brothers were struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 以中書令趙彥深代楊愔總機務。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Zhao Yanshen was made to replace Yang Yin in overseeing critical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat director Zhao Yanshen replaced Yang Yin in overseeing critical affairs.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚少卿陽休之私謂人曰：「將涉千里，殺騏驎而策蹇驢，可悲之甚也！

translations.literal: Palace Reception Vice Director Yang Xiuzhi said privately to someone, "About to cross a thousand li, yet you kill the qilin and drive the lame donkey—how deeply pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: Palace reception vice director Yang Xiuzhi said privately, "About to cross a thousand li, yet you kill the qilin and drive the lame donkey—how pitiable!

sentences.zh: 戊申，演為大丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，湛為太傅、京畿大都督，段韶為大將軍，平陽王淹為太尉，平秦王歸彥為司徒，彭城王浟為尚書令。

translations.literal: On wushen, Yan was made grand chief minister, commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad, and recorder of the masters of writing; Zhan Grand Tutor and metropolitan commander of the capital region; Duan Shao Grand General; Prince Yan of Pingyang Grand Commandant; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin Minister of Works as Minister of Education; Prince You of Pengcheng Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Gao Yan was made grand chief minister, commander-in-chief of all armies, and recorder of the masters of writing; Gao Zhan grand tutor and metropolitan commander of the capital region; Duan Shao grand general; Prince Yan of Pingyang grand commandant; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin minister of education; Prince You of Pengcheng director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 江陵之陷也，長城世子昌及中書侍郎頊皆沒於長安。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, Heir Chang of the Great Wall and Secretariat Gentleman Xu were both lost in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, heir Chen Chang and secretariat gentleman Chen Xu were both captive in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，屢請之於周，周人許而不遣。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he repeatedly requested them from Zhou; Zhou men promised but did not send them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Baxian took the throne he repeatedly requested them from Northern Zhou; the Zhou promised but did not send them.

sentences.zh: 高祖殂，周人乃遣昌還，以王琳之難，居於安陸。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Zhou men then sent Chang back; because of Wang Lin's troubles he dwelt at Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Baxian died, Northern Zhou sent Chen Chang back; because of Wang Lin's campaign he stayed at Anlu.

sentences.zh: 琳敗，昌發安陸，將濟江，致書於上，辭甚不遜。

translations.literal: When Lin was defeated, Chang set out from Anlu and was about to cross the river; he sent a letter to the emperor, its wording very insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin was defeated, Chen Chang set out from Anlu to cross the river and sent a letter to Chen Qian, its wording very insubordinate.

sentences.zh: 上不懌，召侯安都從容謂曰：「太子將至，須別求一籓為歸老之地。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; he summoned Hou Andu and said at ease, "The heir is coming; we must separately seek a fief as a place to retire in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qian was displeased; he summoned Hou Andu and said, "The heir is coming; we must find a fief where I can retire in old age.

sentences.zh: 」安都曰：「自古豈有被代天子！

translations.literal: " Andu said, "Since antiquity has there ever been a Son of Heaven who was replaced!
translations.idiomatic: " Hou Andu said, "Since antiquity has there ever been a Son of Heaven who was replaced!

sentences.zh: 臣愚，不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: Your servant is foolish and dares not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is foolish and dares not accept such an order.

sentences.zh: 」因請自迎昌。

translations.literal: " He thereupon asked to go himself to welcome Chang.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon asked to go himself to welcome Chen Chang.

sentences.zh: 於是群臣上表，請加昌爵命。

translations.literal: Thereupon the hundred officials memorialized, asking that titles and offices be added for Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the ministers memorialized, asking that titles and offices be added for Chen Chang.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以昌為驃騎將軍、湘州牧，封衡陽王。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Chang was made General of Agile Cavalry and Xiangzhou governor, enfeoffed as Prince of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Chen Chang was made general of agile cavalry and Xiangzhou governor, enfeoffed as Prince of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 齊大丞相演如晉陽，既至，謂王晞曰：「不用卿言，幾至傾覆。

translations.literal: Northern Qi's grand chief minister Yan went to Jinyang; when he arrived he said to Wang Xi, "By not using your words I nearly came to overturn.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's grand chief minister Gao Yan went to Jinyang; when he arrived he said to Wang Xi, "By not heeding your words I nearly came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 今君側雖清，終當何以處我？

translations.literal: Now though the ruler's side is clear, in the end how am I to be placed?
translations.idiomatic: Now though the court is clear, in the end what am I to do?

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「殿下往時位地，猶可以名教出處；

translations.literal: " Xi said, "Your Highness's former rank and position could still be governed by name and teaching;
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "Your Highness's former rank could still be governed by name and teaching;

sentences.zh: 今日事勢，遂關天時，非復人理所及。

translations.literal: today's situation and momentum already touch Heaven's season—it is no longer within human reason.
translations.idiomatic: today's situation already touches Heaven's season—it is no longer within human reason.

sentences.zh: 」演奏趙郡王睿為左長史，王晞為司馬。

translations.literal: " He memorialized to install Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery as left chief administrator and Wang Xi as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: " He memorialized to install Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery as left chief administrator and Wang Xi as marshal.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲寅，詔：「軍國之政，皆申晉陽，稟大丞相規算。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiayin, an edict said, "Military and state government are all referred to Jinyang, following the grand chief minister's plans.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiayin, an edict said, "Military and state government are all referred to Jinyang, following the grand chief minister's plans.

sentences.zh: 周軍初至，郢州助防張世貴舉外城以應之，所失軍民三千餘口。

translations.literal: When Zhou troops first arrived, Yingzhou assistant defender Zhang Shigui raised the outer city to join them; lost were more than three thousand soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Zhou troops first arrived, Yingzhou assistant defender Zhang Shigui surrendered the outer city; more than three thousand soldiers and civilians were lost.

sentences.zh: 周人起土山、長梯，晝夜攻之，因風縱火，燒其內城南面五十餘樓。

translations.literal: Zhou men raised earth mounds and long ladders and attacked day and night; they used the wind to set fires and burned more than fifty towers on the south of the inner city's wall.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou raised earth mounds and long ladders and attacked day and night; they used the wind to set fires and burned more than fifty towers on the south of the inner wall.

sentences.zh: 孫瑒兵不滿千人，身自撫循，行酒賦食，士卒皆為之死戰。

translations.literal: Sun Yong's troops were fewer than a thousand; he personally comforted and encouraged them, went among them with wine and distributed food; the soldiers all fought to the death for him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yong had fewer than a thousand men; he personally encouraged them, went among them with wine and food; his soldiers all fought to the death for him.

sentences.zh: 周人不能克，乃授瑒柱國、郢州刺史，封萬戶郡公；

translations.literal: Zhou men could not overcome him; they then invested Yong as Pillar of State and Yingzhou inspector, enfeoffing him as Duke of a Ten-Thousand-Household Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou could not overcome him; they invested Sun Yong as pillar of state and Yingzhou inspector, enfeoffing him as duke of a ten-thousand-household commandery;

sentences.zh: 瑒偽許以緩之，而潛修戰守之備，一朝而具，乃復拒守。

translations.literal: Yong falsely agreed to ease them, but secretly repaired defenses for war and holding; in one morning all was ready, and he again refused and held.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yong falsely agreed to ease them, but secretly repaired defenses; in one morning all was ready, and he held the city again.

sentences.zh: 既而周人聞王琳敗，陳兵將至，乃解圍去。

translations.literal: Before long Zhou men heard Wang Lin was defeated and Chen troops were coming; they then lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Zhou heard Wang Lin was defeated and Chen troops were coming; they lifted the siege and left.

sentences.zh: 瑒集將佐謂之曰：「吾與王公同獎梁室，勤亦至矣。

translations.literal: Yong assembled his generals and aides and said to them, "I and the prince together upheld the Liang house; our diligence has also reached its limit.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yong assembled his officers and said, "I and the prince together upheld the Liang house; our diligence has reached its limit.

sentences.zh: 今時事如此，豈非天乎！

translations.literal: Now the times are thus—is it not Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Now the times are thus—is it not Heaven!

sentences.zh: 」遂遣使奉表，舉中流之地來降。

translations.literal: " He thereupon sent envoys with a memorial, offering the midstream lands in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent envoys with a memorial, offering the midstream lands in surrender to Chen.

sentences.zh: 王琳之東下也，帝征南川兵，江州刺史周迪、高州刺史黃法□帥舟師鈄赴之。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was heading east, the emperor summoned southern river troops; Jiangzhou Inspector Zhou Di and Gaozhou Inspector Huang Fa□ led the fleet in haste to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin was heading east, Chen Qian summoned southern river troops; Jiangzhou inspector Zhou Di and Gaozhou inspector Huang Fa□ led the fleet in haste to join him.

sentences.zh: 熊曇朗據城列艦，塞其中路，迪等與周敷共圍之。

translations.literal: Xiong Tanlang held the city and arrayed ships, blocking the middle route; Di and the rest with Zhou Fu jointly besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Tanlang held the city and arrayed ships, blocking the route; Zhou Di and the rest with Zhou Fu jointly besieged him.

sentences.zh: 琳敗，曇朗部眾離心，迪攻拔其城，虜男女萬餘口。

translations.literal: When Lin was defeated, Tanlang's followers lost heart; Di stormed and took his city and captured more than ten thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin was defeated, Tanlang's followers lost heart; Zhou Di stormed his city and captured more than ten thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 曇朗走入村中，村民斬之；

translations.literal: Tanlang fled into a village; village men beheaded him;
translations.idiomatic: Tanlang fled into a village; villagers beheaded him;

sentences.zh: 丁巳，傳首建康，盡滅其族。

translations.literal: on dingsi his head was sent to Jiankang and his clan was utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: on dingsi his head was sent to Jiankang and his clan was utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 齊軍先守魯山，戊午，棄城走，詔南豫州刺史程靈洗守之。

translations.literal: Qi troops had first garrisoned Lushan; on wuwu they abandoned the city and fled; an edict ordered South Yuzhou Inspector Cheng Lingxi to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi troops had garrisoned Lushan; on wuwu they abandoned the city and fled; an edict ordered South Yuzhou inspector Cheng Lingxi to hold it.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，置武州、沅州，以右衛將軍吳明徹為武州刺史，以孫瑒為湘州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Wuzhou and Yuanzhou were established; Right Guards General Wu Mingche was made Wuzhou inspector; Sun Yong was made Xiangzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Wuzhou and Yuanzhou were established; right guards general Wu Mingche was made Wuzhou inspector; Sun Yong was made Xiangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 瑒懷不自安，固請入朝，征為中領軍；

translations.literal: Yong felt insecure in his mind and firmly asked to enter court; he was summoned as Central Garrison-general;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yong felt insecure and asked to enter court; he was summoned as central garrison-general;

sentences.zh: 未拜，除吳郡太守。

translations.literal: before he took office he was appointed Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: before he took office he was appointed administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 壬申，齊封世宗之子孝珩為廣寧王，長恭為蘭陵王。

translations.literal: On renshen, Qi enfeoffed Shizong's sons Xiaoxing as Prince of Guangning and Changgong as Prince of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Northern Qi enfeoffed Gao Yin's sons Xiaoxing as Prince of Guangning and Changgong as Prince of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，衡陽獻王昌入境，詔主書、舍人緣道迎候；

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Prince Xian of Hengyang Chang entered the borders; an edict ordered chief clerks and attendants along the route to welcome him;
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Prince Xian of Hengyang Chen Chang entered the borders; an edict ordered clerks and attendants along the route to welcome him;

sentences.zh: 丙子，濟江，中流，隕之，使以溺告。

translations.literal: on bingzi he crossed the river; midstream he fell; they reported it as drowning.
translations.idiomatic: on bingzi he crossed the river; midstream he fell; they reported it as drowning.

sentences.zh: 侯安都以功進爵清遠公。

translations.literal: Hou Andu for his merit was advanced in rank to Duke of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Andu for his merit was advanced to Duke of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖遣滎陽毛喜從安成王頊詣江陵，梁世祖以喜為侍郎，沒於長安，與昌俱還，因進和親之策。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gaozu had sent Mao Xi of Xingyang to follow Prince of Ancheng Xu to Jiangling; Liang Emperor Yuan made Xi vice director; he was lost in Chang'an, returned with Chang, and thereupon advanced a policy of marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chen Baxian had sent Mao Xi of Xingyang to follow Prince of Ancheng Chen Xu to Jiangling; Liang Emperor Yuan made him vice director; he was captive in Chang'an, returned with Chen Chang, and advanced a policy of marriage alliance with Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 上乃使侍中周弘正通好於周。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent Palace Attendant Zhou Hongzheng to open good relations with Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qian then sent palace attendant Zhou Hongzheng to open good relations with Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁亥，立皇子伯信為衡陽王，奉獻王祀。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dinghai, the emperor installed his son Boxin as Prince of Hengyang to carry Prince Xian's sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dinghai, Chen Qian installed his son Boxin as Prince of Hengyang to carry Chen Chang's sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 周世宗明敏有識量，晉公護憚之，使膳部中大夫李安置毒於糖食追而進之。

translations.literal: Zhou Shizong was bright and keen in judgment; Duke of Jin Hu feared him and had Chief of Provisions Li An place poison in sugared food and pursue to present it.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou's Yuwen Yu was bright and keen in judgment; Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu feared him and had Li An of the provisions bureau place poison in sugared food and present it.

sentences.zh: 帝頗覺之，庚子，大漸，口授遺詔五百餘言，且曰：「朕子年幼，未堪當國。

translations.literal: The emperor was somewhat aware; on gengzi he was critically ill; he dictated by mouth a final edict of more than five hundred words and said, "My sons are young and cannot yet bear the state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was somewhat aware; on gengzi he was critically ill; he dictated a final edict of more than five hundred words and said, "My sons are young and cannot yet bear the state.

sentences.zh: 魯公，朕之介弟，寬仁大度，海內共聞；

translations.literal: The Duke of Lu is my younger brother by the same mother, broad and humane in magnanimity, known throughout the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Lu is my younger brother by the same mother, broad and humane, known throughout the realm;

sentences.zh: 能弘我周家，必此子也。

translations.literal: he can expand our Zhou house—surely this son.
translations.idiomatic: he can expand our Zhou house—surely this son.

sentences.zh: 」辛丑，殂。

translations.literal: " On xinchou he died.
translations.idiomatic: " On xinchou he died.

sentences.zh: 魯公幼有器質，特為世宗所親愛，朝廷大事，多與之參議；

translations.literal: The Duke of Lu from youth had capacity and quality, was especially loved by Shizong, and on great court affairs often deliberated with him;
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Yong from youth had capacity and quality, was especially loved by Yuwen Yu, and on great court affairs often deliberated with him;

sentences.zh: 性深沉，有遠識，非因顧問，終不輒言。

translations.literal: his nature was deep and reserved, with far sight; unless consulted he never spoke rashly.
translations.idiomatic: his nature was deep and reserved, with far sight; unless consulted he never spoke rashly.

sentences.zh: 世宗每歎曰：「夫人不言，言必有中。

translations.literal: Shizong often sighed and said, "When this man does not speak, if he speaks it surely hits the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Yu often sighed and said, "When this man does not speak, if he speaks it surely hits the mark.

sentences.zh: 」壬寅，魯公即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: " On renyin the Duke of Lu took the emperor's throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: " On renyin Yuwen Yong took the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬子，齊以開府儀同三司劉洪徽為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renzi, Qi made Acting Three Excellencies Liu Honghui Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renzi, Northern Qi made Liu Honghui, equal in honor to the three dukes, right vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 侯安都父文捍為始興內史，卒官。

translations.literal: Hou Andu's father Wenhan was Administrator of Shixing Interior; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Andu's father Wenhan was administrator of Shixing Interior; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 上迎其母還建康，母固求停鄉里。

translations.literal: The emperor welcomed his mother back to Jiankang; the mother firmly asked to remain in her home district.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qian welcomed his mother back to Jiankang; she firmly asked to remain in her home district.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，為置東衡州，以安都從弟曉為刺史；

translations.literal: On yimao, Eastern Hengzhou was established for her; Andu's younger cousin Xiao was made inspector;
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Eastern Hengzhou was established for her; Hou Andu's younger cousin Xiao was made inspector;

sentences.zh: 安都子秘，才九歲，上以為始興內史，並令在鄉侍養。

translations.literal: Andu's son Mi was only nine years old; the emperor made him Administrator of Shixing Interior and ordered both to remain in the district to attend and nourish her.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Andu's son Mi was only nine; Chen Qian made him administrator of Shixing Interior and ordered both to remain in the district to attend her.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬辰，詔葬梁元帝於江寧，車旗禮章，悉用梁典。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renchen, an edict buried Liang Emperor Yuan at Jiangning; chariots, banners, rites, and regalia all followed Liang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renchen, an edict buried Liang Emperor Yuan at Jiangning with all Liang rites and regalia.

sentences.zh: 齊人收永安、上黨二王遣骨，葬之。

translations.literal: Qi men collected the dispatched bones of the two princes of Yong'an and Shangdang and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi collected the remains of the two princes of Yong'an and Shangdang and buried them.

sentences.zh: 敕上黨王妃李氏還第。

translations.literal: An order returned Princess Li of Shangdang to her residence.
translations.idiomatic: An order returned Princess Li of Shangdang to her residence.

sentences.zh: 馮文洛尚以故意，修飾詣之。

translations.literal: Feng Wenluo still held old intent and went to her adorned.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Wenluo still held old intent and went to her in full dress.

sentences.zh: 妃盛列左右，立文洛於階下，數之曰：「遭難流離，以至大辱，志操寡薄，不能自盡。

translations.literal: The princess arrayed attendants left and right, set Wenluo on the steps below, and rebuked him, saying, "Suffering hardship and exile, I came to great disgrace; my will and conduct were thin, and I could not end myself.
translations.idiomatic: The princess arrayed her attendants on either side, set Wenluo on the steps below, and rebuked him: "Through hardship and exile I came to great disgrace; my will was too weak, and I could not die with honor.

sentences.zh: 幸蒙恩詔，得反籓闈，汝何物奴，猶欲見侮！

translations.literal: By fortune I received an imperial grace and could return to the princely household—what sort of slave are you, that you still wish to insult me!
translations.idiomatic: By grace of the throne I was allowed to return to my husband's house—what sort of slave are you, that you still dare insult me!

sentences.zh: 」杖之一百，血流灑地。

translations.literal: " She beat him one hundred strokes; blood flowed and pooled on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: " She had him beaten a hundred strokes until blood pooled on the ground.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙辰，封皇子伯山為鄱陽王。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on bingchen, Prince Boshan was enfeoffed as King of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, on bingchen, Prince Boshan was enfeoffed as king of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 齊丞相演以王晞儒緩，恐不允武將之意，每夜載入，晝則不與語。

translations.literal: Qi chancellor Yan, because Wang Xi was scholarly and slow, feared he would not satisfy the martial commanders' intent; each night he brought him in by carriage, but by day did not speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi chancellor Yan thought Wang Xi too bookish and slow to satisfy the generals; each night he had him brought in by carriage, yet by day would not speak with him.

sentences.zh: 嘗進晞密室，謂曰：「比王侯諸貴，每見敦迫，言我違天不祥，恐當或有變起。

translations.literal: Once he led Xi into a secret chamber and said, "Lately the princes and nobles, whenever they see me, press hard, saying I defy Heaven and bring ill fortune—they fear some upheaval may arise.
translations.idiomatic: Once he led Xi into a secret chamber and said, "Lately every prince and noble I meet presses me hard, saying I defy Heaven and court disaster—they fear rebellion is brewing.

sentences.zh: 吾欲以法繩之，何如？

translations.literal: I wish to bind them by law—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: I mean to bring them to law—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「朝廷比者疏遠親戚，殿下倉猝所行，非復人臣之事。

translations.literal: " Xi said, "The court of late has kept kin at a distance; what Your Highness did in haste is no longer the affair of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi said, "The court has lately kept its kin at arm's length; what Your Highness did in haste is no longer the conduct of a subject.

sentences.zh: 芒刺在背，上下相疑，何由可久！

translations.literal: A thorn in the back—above and below suspect each other; how can this last long!
translations.idiomatic: It is like a thorn in the back—ruler and subject eye each other with suspicion; how can such a state endure?

sentences.zh: 殿下雖欲謙退，秕糠神器，實恐違上玄之意，墜先帝之基。

translations.literal: Though Your Highness wishes to yield humbly, to treat the sacred vessel as chaff truly fears violating Heaven's intent and toppling the late emperor's foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Highness wishes to step aside, to treat the throne as chaff would violate Heaven's will and topple your father's house.

sentences.zh: 」演曰：「卿何敢發此言，須致卿於法！

translations.literal: " Yan said, "How dare you speak such words—I must bring you to law!
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said, "How dare you speak such words—I ought to have you punished by law!

sentences.zh: 」秕曰：「天時人事，皆無異謀，是以敢冒犯斧鉞，抑亦神明所贊耳。

translations.literal: " Pi said, "Heaven's season and human affairs show no other design; therefore I dare offend the axe and halberd—yet this is also what the spirits approve.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi said, "Heaven and the times alike point one way; that is why I dare risk your wrath—and surely the spirits approve.

sentences.zh: 」演曰：「拯難匡時，方俟聖哲，吾何敢私議！

translations.literal: " Yan said, "To rescue hardship and set the age right awaits a sage—I how dare speak in private!
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said, "To save the realm awaits a sage—I am no one to plot in private!

sentences.zh: 幸勿多言！

translations.literal: Pray speak no more!
translations.idiomatic: Say no more!

sentences.zh: 」丞相從事中郎陸杳將出使，握晞手，使之勸進。

translations.literal: " Chancellor Attendant Gentleman Lu Yao was about to go on a mission; he grasped Xi's hand and had him urge Yan to advance.
translations.idiomatic: " Chancellor attendant gentleman Lu Yao, about to depart on a mission, took Xi's hand and bade him urge Yan to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 晞以杳言告演，演曰：「若內外鹹有此意，趙彥深朝夕左右，何故初無一言？

translations.literal: Xi told Yan what Yao had said; Yan said, "If inside and outside alike hold this intent, Zhao Yanshen is at my side morning and night—why has he never spoken a word?
translations.idiomatic: Xi relayed Yao's words; Yan said, "If court and camp alike feel this way, Zhao Yanshen is at my side day and night—why has he never said a word?

sentences.zh: 」晞乃以事隙密問彥深，彥深曰：「我比亦驚此聲論，每欲陳聞，則口噤心悸。

translations.literal: " Xi then in a spare moment secretly asked Yanshen; Yanshen said, "I too have been startled by this talk; each time I wished to report it, my mouth sealed shut and my heart pounded.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi then stole a moment to ask Yanshen privately; Yanshen said, "This talk alarms me too; whenever I mean to speak, my throat closes and my heart pounds.

sentences.zh: 弟既發端，吾亦當昧死一披肝膽。

translations.literal: Since you, my younger brother, have opened the matter, I too ought to risk death and lay bare my liver and heart.
translations.idiomatic: Since you have broached it, I too will risk death and speak my mind.

sentences.zh: 」因共勸演。

translations.literal: " Thereupon together they urged Yan.
translations.idiomatic: " Together they pressed Yan forward.

sentences.zh: 演遂言於太皇太后。

translations.literal: Yan then spoke to the grand empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then laid the matter before the grand empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 趙道德曰：「相王不效周公輔成王，而欲骨肉相奪，不畏後世謂之篡邪？

translations.literal: Zhao Daode said, "The prince does not imitate the Duke of Zhou assisting King Cheng, but wishes kin to seize from kin—does he not fear posterity will call it usurpation?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Daode said, "The prince would not play the Duke of Zhou to a young king, but would seize the throne from his own blood—does he not fear posterity will call it usurpation?

sentences.zh: 」太皇太后曰：「道德之言是也。

translations.literal: " The grand empress dowager said, "Daode's words are right.
translations.idiomatic: " The grand empress dowager said, "Daode speaks rightly.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，演又啟云：「天下人心未定，恐奄忽變生，須早定名位。

translations.literal: " Before long Yan again memorialized, saying, "The hearts of the realm are not settled; I fear sudden change—the title must be fixed early.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Yan memorialized again: "The realm is unsettled; sudden disaster may come—we must fix the succession at once.

sentences.zh: 」太皇太后乃從之。

translations.literal: " The grand empress dowager then consented.
translations.idiomatic: " The grand empress dowager yielded.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬午，太皇太后下令，廢齊主為濟南王，出居別宮，以常山王演入纂大統，且戒之曰：「勿令濟南有他也！

translations.literal: Eighth month, on renwu, the grand empress dowager issued an order deposing the Qi ruler as Prince of Jinan, sending him to dwell in a separate palace, and installing Prince Yan of Changshan to succeed the great line; she also admonished him, saying, "Do not let Jinan come to other harm!
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, on renwu, the grand empress dowager deposed the Qi ruler as prince of Jinan and sent him to a separate palace, installing Prince Yan of Changshan on the throne; she warned him: "Do not let harm come again to Jinan!

sentences.zh: 肅宗即皇帝位於晉陽，大赦，改元皇建。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong took the throne at Jinyang, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Huangjian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong took the throne at Jinyang, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Huangjian.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后還稱皇太后；

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager again took the title empress dowager;
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager resumed the title of empress dowager;

sentences.zh: 皇太后稱文宣皇后，宮曰昭信。

translations.literal: the empress dowager was titled Empress Wensuan, her palace called Zhaoxin.
translations.idiomatic: the empress dowager was titled Empress Wensuan, her residence called Zhaoxin.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔紹封功臣，禮賜耆老，延訪直言，褒賞死事，追贈名德。

translations.literal: On yiyou, an edict continued enfeoffments for meritorious ministers, honored the aged with ritual gifts, sought forthright counsel, rewarded those who died in service, and posthumously ennobled men of famed virtue.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, an edict renewed enfeoffments for meritorious ministers, honored the aged, sought blunt counsel, rewarded the war dead, and posthumously ennobled men of renown.

sentences.zh: 帝謂王晞曰：「卿何為自同外客，略不可見？

translations.literal: The emperor said to Wang Xi, "Why do you make yourself like an outside guest—hardly to be seen at all?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Wang Xi, "Why do you hold yourself aloof like a stranger—I scarcely see you?

sentences.zh: 自今假非局司，但有所懷，隨宜作一牒，俟少隙，即徑進也。

translations.literal: From now on, even if not of the regular staff, whenever you have something in mind, draft a note as fits and, when a brief opening appears, bring it straight in.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter, even if you are not on the regular staff, whenever something weighs on you, write a note and, the moment you find an opening, bring it straight to me.

sentences.zh: 」因敕晞與尚書陽休之、鴻臚卿崔晞等三人，每日職務罷，並入東廊，共舉錄歷代禮樂、職官及田市、徵稅，或不便於時而相承施用，或自古為利而於今廢墜，或道德高俊，久在沉淪，或巧言眩俗，妖邪害政者，悉令詳思，以漸條奏。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Xi together with Secretariat Director Yang Xiuzhi, Chamberlain for Dependencies Cui Xi, and three others—each day when duties ended, all to enter the eastern gallery and jointly compile records of ritual and music, offices, fields and markets, and levies through the ages: what was inconvenient to the times yet still applied by succession, what had been profitable since antiquity yet was now abandoned, what men of lofty virtue had long lain submerged, or what clever words dazzled the vulgar and demonic harm afflicted government—all were to ponder in detail and memorialize item by item.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered Xi, together with Yang Xiuzhi of the Secretariat, Cui Xi the chamberlain for dependencies, and one other: each day after court they were to meet in the eastern gallery and compile, era by era, ritual and music, offices, land and markets, and taxes—what custom kept though ill-suited to the age, what ancient profit lay in ruins, what worthy men languished forgotten, what slick tongues misled the people and what evil harmed the state—and report their findings in orderly memorials.

sentences.zh: 朝晡給御食，畢景聽還。

translations.literal: Morning and evening imperial food was provided; when the day closed they were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: They were fed from the imperial kitchen morning and evening, and dismissed at day's end.

sentences.zh: 帝識度沉敏，少居台閣，明習吏事，即位，尤自勤勵，大革顯祖之弊，時人服其明而譏其細。

translations.literal: The emperor's discernment was deep and keen; in youth he dwelt in the terrace offices, clearly versed in clerical affairs; on taking the throne he was especially self-diligent, greatly reforming the abuses of Emperor Xianzu; men of the time admired his clarity yet mocked his minuteness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deep-minded and sharp; raised in the central offices, he knew administration well; once enthroned he drove himself harder still, sweeping away Xianzu's abuses—men admired his clarity but mocked his fussiness.

sentences.zh: 嘗問舍人裴澤，在外議論得失。

translations.literal: Once he asked Attendant Gentleman Pei Ze what was said outside of right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Once he asked attendant gentleman Pei Ze what people said of him outside court.

sentences.zh: 澤率爾對曰：「陛下陪明至公，自可遠侔古昔；

translations.literal: Ze answered straight off, saying, "Your Majesty's brilliance and utmost fairness can themselves match the ancients from afar;
translations.idiomatic: Ze answered without hesitation: "Your Majesty's brilliance and fairness could rival the ancients;

sentences.zh: 而有識之士，鹹言傷細，帝王之度，頗為未弘。

translations.literal: yet men of insight all say you wound with minuteness—the measure of an emperor is rather not yet broad.
translations.idiomatic: yet thoughtful men all say you wound with minuteness—the breadth of an emperor's manner is still wanting.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「誠如卿言。

translations.literal: " The emperor smiled and said, "Truly as you say.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor smiled. "You are right.

sentences.zh: 朕初臨萬機，慮不周悉，故致爾耳。

translations.literal: When I first faced the myriad duties, my concern was not thorough, and so this came about.
translations.idiomatic: When I first took the reins I feared to miss anything, and so became petty.

sentences.zh: 此事安可久行，恐後又嫌疏漏。

translations.literal: This matter—how can it long continue? I fear later they will blame laxness.
translations.idiomatic: That cannot go on; later they will call me careless.

sentences.zh: 」澤由是被寵遇。

translations.literal: " Ze thereby received favor.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on Ze enjoyed the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 庫狄顯安侍坐，帝曰：「顯安，我姑之子；

translations.literal: Kudi Xian'an sat in attendance; the emperor said, "Xian'an, son of my aunt;
translations.idiomatic: Kudi Xian'an sat with him; the emperor said, "Xian'an, you are my cousin's son;

sentences.zh: 今序家人禮，除君臣之敬，可言我之不逮。

translations.literal: now we follow family rites and set aside the respect between ruler and minister—you may speak where I fall short.
translations.idiomatic: today we set aside court form and speak as kin—tell me where I fail.

sentences.zh: 」顯安曰：「陛下多妄言。

translations.literal: " Xian'an said, "Your Majesty speaks much that is untrue.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian'an said, "Your Majesty talks much nonsense.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「何故？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "For what reason?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "How so?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下昔見文宣以馬鞭撻人，常以為非；

translations.literal: " He answered, "Your Majesty once saw Wensuan beat men with a horsewhip and always held it wrong;
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Your Majesty once condemned Wensuan for beating men with a horsewhip;

sentences.zh: 今自行之，非妄言邪？

translations.literal: now you do it yourself—is that not untrue speech?
translations.idiomatic: now you do the same—is that not nonsense?

sentences.zh: 」帝握其手謝之。

translations.literal: " The emperor grasped his hand and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took his hand and apologized.

sentences.zh: 又使直言，對曰：「陛下太細，天子乃更似吏。

translations.literal: He again bade blunt speech; the answer was, "Your Majesty is too minute—the Son of Heaven comes to resemble a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for more blunt counsel; Xian'an said, "Your Majesty is too fussy—a Son of Heaven ends up looking like a clerk.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕甚知之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "I know it very well.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I know it well.

sentences.zh: 然無法日久，將整之以至無為耳。

translations.literal: Yet long without law, I will set things in order until there is non-action.
translations.idiomatic: But the realm has long gone without law; I mean to tighten discipline until order needs no forcing.

sentences.zh: 」又問王晞，晞曰：「顯安言是也。

translations.literal: " He again asked Wang Xi; Xi said, "Xian'an speaks rightly.
translations.idiomatic: " He asked Wang Xi, who said, "Xian'an is right.

sentences.zh: 」顯安，干之子也。

translations.literal: " Xian'an was son of Gan.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian'an was a son of Gan.

sentences.zh: 群臣進言，帝皆從容受納。

translations.literal: When ministers advanced counsel, the emperor always received it calmly.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever ministers offered, the emperor heard with grace.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，太后不豫，帝行不能正履，容色貶悴，衣不解帶殆將四旬。

translations.literal: His nature was utmost filial; when the empress dowager was unwell, the emperor could not walk with proper step, his countenance wan and haggard, his garments unloosed at the belt for nearly forty days.
translations.idiomatic: He was profoundly filial: when the empress dowager fell ill he could scarcely walk upright, his face gaunt, his belt unloosed for nearly forty days.
