sentences.zh: 太后疾小增，即寢伏閣外，食飲藥物，皆手親之。

translations.literal: When her illness worsened slightly, he at once slept prostrate outside her chamber; food, drink, and medicine—all he attended with his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: When her illness sharpened he slept on the floor outside her door and with his own hands brought every meal and dose of medicine.

sentences.zh: 太后嘗心痛不自堪，帝立侍帷前，以爪掐掌代痛，血流出袖。

translations.literal: Once the empress dowager's heart pained her beyond bearing; the emperor stood attending before the curtain, scoring his palm with his nails in place of her pain—blood ran down his sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: Once her heart pained her unbearably; the emperor stood by the curtain and raked his own palms with his nails as though to take her pain—blood soaked his sleeves.

sentences.zh: 友愛諸弟，無君臣之隔。

translations.literal: He was affectionate toward his younger brothers, without the barrier of ruler and subject.
translations.idiomatic: He loved his younger brothers without the chill of throne and subject.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以長廣王湛為右丞相，平陽王淹為太傅，彭城王浟為大司馬。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Prince Zhan of Changgung was made Right Chancellor, Prince Yan of Pingyang Grand Tutor, and Prince You of Pengcheng Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Prince Zhan of Changgung was made right chancellor, Prince Yan of Pingyang grand tutor, and Prince You of Pengcheng grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 周軍司馬賀若敦，帥眾一萬，奄至武陵；

translations.literal: Zhou army marshal He Ruo Dun led ten thousand men and suddenly reached Wuling;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou army marshal He Ruo Dun led ten thousand men in a sudden strike on Wuling;

sentences.zh: 武州刺史吳明徹不能拒，引軍還巴陵。

translations.literal: Wuzhou Inspector Wu Mingche could not resist and led his army back to Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou inspector Wu Mingche could not hold and withdrew to Baling.

sentences.zh: 江陵之陷也，巴、湘之地盡入於周，周使梁人守之。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, the lands of Ba and Xiang all passed to Zhou; Zhou had men of Liang guard them.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangling fell, Ba and Xiang had passed to Zhou, which set Liang men to garrison them.

sentences.zh: 太尉侯瑱等將兵逼湘州。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Hou Tian and others led troops to press Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand marshal Hou Tian marched on Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 賀若敦將步騎救之，乘勝深入，軍於湘川。

translations.literal: He Ruo Dun led infantry and cavalry to rescue it, pressing the victory in deep, and encamped on the Xiang River.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruo Dun marched infantry and cavalry to relieve the city, pursued his advantage deep inland, and camped on the Xiang.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙卯，周將獨孤盛將水軍與敦俱進。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on yimao, Zhou general Dugu Sheng led the water army forward with Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, on yimao, Zhou general Dugu Sheng advanced by river with Dun.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，遣儀同三司徐度將兵會侯瑱於巴丘。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank Xu Du was sent with troops to join Hou Tian at Baqiu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, palace attendant of the third rank Xu Du was sent to join Hou Tian at Baqiu.

sentences.zh: 會秋水泛溢，盛、敦糧援斷絕，分軍抄掠，以供資費。

translations.literal: As autumn waters flooded wide, Sheng and Dun's grain and supplies were cut off; they divided troops to raid and forage for expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn floods cut Sheng and Dun off from supplies; they split their forces to raid the countryside for food.

sentences.zh: 敦恐瑱知其糧少，乃於營內多為土聚，覆之以米，召旁村人，陽有訪問，隨即遣之。

translations.literal: Dun feared Tian would know his grain was few; he therefore made many earthen mounds in camp, covered them with rice, summoned villagers nearby, pretended to question them, and at once sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Dun feared Tian would learn how short he was of grain; inside camp he heaped earth and spread rice on top, called in nearby villagers under pretense of questioning them, then sent them away at once.

sentences.zh: 瑱聞之，良以為實。

translations.literal: Tian heard of it and took it fully for truth.
translations.idiomatic: Tian took the ruse for truth.

sentences.zh: 敦又增修營壘，造廬舍為久留之計，湘、羅之間遂廢農業。

translations.literal: Dun again strengthened ramparts and built huts as a plan for long stay; between Xiang and Luo agriculture was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Dun strengthened his walls and built huts as though settling in for a siege; farming between the Xiang and Luo ceased.

sentences.zh: 瑱等無如之何。

translations.literal: Tian and the rest could do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tian could find no answer.

sentences.zh: 先是土人亟乘輕船，載米粟雞鴨以餉瑱軍。

translations.literal: Earlier the local people had often taken light boats loaded with grain, millet, chickens, and ducks to supply Tian's army.
translations.idiomatic: Until then locals had often poled light boats laden with grain and fowl to Tian's camp.

sentences.zh: 敦患之，乃偽為土人裝船，伏甲士於中。

translations.literal: Dun was troubled by this; he therefore disguised boats as local craft and hid armored men within.
translations.idiomatic: Dun countered by fitting out boats like local supply craft and hiding armored men inside.

sentences.zh: 瑱軍人望見，謂餉船之至，逆來爭取，敦甲士出而擒之。

translations.literal: Tian's soldiers saw them, thought supply boats had come, went to meet and seize them, and Dun's armored men sprang out and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Tian's men sighted them, thought provisions had arrived, rushed to seize the boats, and Dun's soldiers burst out and took them.

sentences.zh: 又敦軍數有叛人乘馬投瑱者，敦乃別取一馬，牽以趣船，令船中逆以鞭鞭之。

translations.literal: Again Dun's army had many deserters who rode horses to Tian; Dun therefore took another horse, led it toward a boat, and had men in the boat whip it from below.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Dun's men had deserted on horseback to Tian; Dun took another horse, led it to a boat, and had sailors below whip it from underneath.

sentences.zh: 如是者再三，馬畏船不上。

translations.literal: Thus several times—the horse feared the boat and would not board.
translations.idiomatic: He did this again and again until the horse feared boats and would not board.

sentences.zh: 然後伏兵於江岸，使人乘畏船馬以招瑱軍，詐雲投附。

translations.literal: Then he set ambush on the riverbank, had a man ride the boat-fearing horse to entice Tian's army, falsely claiming defection.
translations.idiomatic: Then he hid troops on the bank and sent a man on the frightened horse to lure Tian's men, pretending to defect.

sentences.zh: 瑱遣兵迎接，競來牽馬，馬既畏船不上，伏兵發，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Tian sent troops to welcome them; they vied to seize the horse; the horse, fearing the boat, would not board; the ambush sprang forth and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Tian sent men to welcome the rider; they crowded to seize the horse; it would not board; the ambush rose and slaughtered them all.

sentences.zh: 此後實有饋餉及亡降者，瑱猶謂之詐，並拒擊之。

translations.literal: After this, even when there were real supplies and real deserters, Tian still took them for deceit and rejected or struck them.
translations.idiomatic: After that, even real supplies and real deserters Tian treated as tricks and drove away.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸巳，瑱襲破獨孤盛於楊葉洲，盛收兵登岸，築城自保。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on guisi, Tian raided and broke Dugu Sheng at Yangye Isle; Sheng gathered troops ashore and built a fort to hold himself.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, on guisi, Hou Tian smashed Dugu Sheng at Yangye Isle; Sheng pulled his men ashore and walled himself in.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔司空侯安都帥眾會瑱南討。

translations.literal: On dingyou, an edict ordered Minister of Works Hou Andu to lead troops to join Tian in the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, an edict ordered minister of works Hou Andu to join Hou Tian in the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛亥，齊主立妃元氏為皇后，世子百年為太子。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on xinhai, the Qi ruler established Consort Yuan as empress and heir apparent Bainian as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, on xinhai, the Qi ruler made Consort Yuan empress and his heir Bainian crown prince.

sentences.zh: 百年時才五歲。

translations.literal: Bainian was then only five years old.
translations.idiomatic: Bainian was only five.

sentences.zh: 齊主征前開府長史盧叔虎為中庶子。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler summoned former chief clerk of the open mansion Lu Shuhu as palace companion to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler summoned former open-mansion chief clerk Lu Shuhu as tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 叔虎，柔之從叔也。

translations.literal: Shuhu was younger cousin of Rou on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Shuhu was a cousin of Lu Rou.

sentences.zh: 帝問時務於叔虎，叔虎請伐周，曰：「我強彼弱，我富彼貧，其勢相懸。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Shuhu about affairs of the time; Shuhu urged war on Zhou, saying, "We are strong, they weak; we rich, they poor—the disparity of force is vast.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Shuhu's view of the times; Shuhu urged war on Zhou: "We are strong where they are weak, rich where they are poor—the imbalance is extreme.

sentences.zh: 然干戈不息，未能併吞者，此失於不用強富也。

translations.literal: Yet arms do not cease and we cannot swallow them—this is failure to use our strength and wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet war drags on without conquest because we fail to use that strength and wealth.

sentences.zh: 輕兵野戰，勝負難必，是胡騎之法，非萬全之術也。

translations.literal: Light troops in field battle—victory and defeat hard to fix—this is the method of Hu horsemen, not a plan of full security.
translations.idiomatic: Light raids and open battle leave the outcome in doubt—that is nomad warfare, not a sure path.

sentences.zh: 宜立重鎮於平陽，與彼蒲州相對，深溝高壘，運糧積甲。

translations.literal: We ought to establish a heavy fortress at Pingyang opposite their Puzhou, with deep moats and high ramparts, transporting grain and storing armor.
translations.idiomatic: Establish a great fortress at Pingyang facing their Puzhou, dig deep moats, raise high walls, stock grain and armor.

sentences.zh: 彼閉關不出，則稍蠶食其河東之地，日使窮蹙。

translations.literal: If they close the passes and do not come out, we shall little by little devour their Hedong lands and daily drive them to extremity.
translations.idiomatic: If they shut their gates, nibble away at Hedong day by day until they are cornered.

sentences.zh: 若彼出兵，非十萬以上，不足為我敵。

translations.literal: If they send troops, unless above one hundred thousand they are not enough to be our match.
translations.idiomatic: If they march out, it will take more than a hundred thousand to stand against us.

sentences.zh: 所損糧食鹹出關中。

translations.literal: The grain they lose will all come out of Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Every bushel they spend will drain Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 我軍士年別一代，谷食豐饒。

translations.literal: Our soldiers rotate each year; grain is abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Our troops rotate yearly; our granaries overflow.

sentences.zh: 彼來求戰，我則不應；

translations.literal: When they come seeking battle, we do not answer;
translations.idiomatic: If they seek battle, we refuse;

sentences.zh: 彼若退去，我乘其弊。

translations.literal: if they withdraw, we ride their exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: if they withdraw, we strike their weakness.

sentences.zh: 自長安以西，民疏城遠，敵兵來往，實自艱難，與我相持，農業且廢，不過三年，彼自破矣。

translations.literal: West of Chang'an the people are sparse and cities far; enemy troops coming and going are in truth hard pressed; locked with us, agriculture will waste; within three years they will break themselves.
translations.idiomatic: West of Chang'an the land is thin and cities few; every march exhausts them; locked with us, their fields will lie fallow—in three years they will break of themselves.

sentences.zh: 」帝深善之。

translations.literal: " The emperor greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 齊主自將擊庫莫奚，至天池，庫莫奚出長城北遁。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler personally led an attack on the Kumo Xi, reached Tianchi; the Kumo Xi went out beyond the Long Wall and fled north.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler led a campaign against the Kumo Xi as far as Tianchi; they fled north beyond the Long Wall.

sentences.zh: 齊主分兵追擊，獲牛羊七萬而還。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler divided troops in pursuit and returned with seventy thousand cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: He sent columns in pursuit and returned with seventy thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙未，詔：「自今孟春訖於夏首，大辟事已款者，宜且申停。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on yiwei, an edict: "From now, from early spring until the start of summer, capital cases already confessed should for the time being be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, on yiwei, an edict: "From early spring through the start of summer, even confessed capital cases are to be stayed for the season.

sentences.zh: 己亥，周巴陵城主尉遲憲降，遣巴州刺史侯安鼎守之。

translations.literal: On jihai, Zhou Baling city chief Yuchi Xian surrendered; Bazhou Inspector Hou Anding was sent to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Zhou's Baling garrison commander Yuchi Xian surrendered; Hou Anding was sent as inspector of Bazhou to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 庚子，獨孤盛將餘眾自楊葉洲潛遁。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Dugu Sheng led his remaining troops in secret flight from Yangye Isle.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Dugu Sheng stole away with his remnant force from Yangye Isle.

sentences.zh: 丙午，齊主還晉陽。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the Qi ruler returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the Qi ruler returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 齊主斬人於前，問王晞曰：「是人應死不？

translations.literal: The Qi ruler beheaded a man before him and asked Wang Xi, "Should this man die?
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler executed a man in his presence and asked Wang Xi, "Did this man deserve death?

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「應死，但恨死不得其地耳。

translations.literal: " Xi said, "He should die—only I regret he did not die in the proper place.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi said, "He deserved death—but not here.

sentences.zh: 臣聞『刑人於市，與眾棄之。

translations.literal: I have heard, 'Punish men in the market and abandon them with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that punishment belongs in the marketplace, where the people may witness and renounce the criminal.

sentences.zh: 』殿廷非行戮之所。

translations.literal: ' The palace hall is not the place for executions.
translations.idiomatic: The throne hall is no place for killing.

sentences.zh: 」帝改容謝曰：「自今當為王公改之。

translations.literal: " The emperor changed countenance and apologized, saying, "From now on I shall change this for the sake of princes and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's face changed; he apologized: "Hereafter I shall mend my ways—for your sake and for all the princes.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以晞為侍郎，苦辭不受。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Xi a vice director; he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make Xi a vice director of the Secretariat; Xi refused firmly.

sentences.zh: 或勸晞勿自疏，晞曰：「我少年以來，閱要人多矣。

translations.literal: Some urged Xi not to keep himself distant; Xi said, "Since my youth I have seen many men in power.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him not to hold himself aloof; Xi said, "Since youth I have watched many men at the summit of power.

sentences.zh: 得志少時，鮮不顛覆。

translations.literal: Those who gained their aim in youth—few did not overturn.
translations.idiomatic: Few who rise young keep their footing.

sentences.zh: 且吾性實疏緩，不堪時務，人主恩私，何由可保！

translations.literal: Moreover my nature is truly loose and slow—I cannot bear affairs of the time; a ruler's private favor—how can it be kept!
translations.idiomatic: My nature is too easy and slow for court; a ruler's private favor—how could it last?

sentences.zh: 萬一披猖，求退無地。

translations.literal: If by chance things run wild, there will be no place to seek retreat.
translations.idiomatic: If fortune turns, there will be nowhere to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 非不好作要官，但思之爛熟耳。

translations.literal: It is not that I do not wish to hold great office—I have only thought it through to rottenness.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I scorn high office—I have chewed the thought until it is threadbare.

sentences.zh: 初，齊顯祖之末，谷糴踴貴。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Qi Emperor Xianzu, grain prices soared.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xianzu's reign grain prices soared.

sentences.zh: 濟南王即位，尚書左丞蘇珍芝建議修石鱉等屯，自是淮南軍防足食。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jinan took the throne, Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Su Zhenzhi proposed restoring the Shibie and other colonies; from this the Huainan garrisons had full food.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince of Jinan took the throne, left assistant director Su Zhenzhi proposed restoring the Shibie garrison farms; thereafter Huainan's armies ate their fill.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，平州刺史嵇曄建議，開督亢陂，置屯田，歲收稻粟數十萬石，北境周贍。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne, Pingzhou Inspector Ji Ye proposed opening the Dukang reservoir and establishing military colonies; each year several hundred thousand piculs of rice were harvested and the northern frontier was fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong took the throne, Pingzhou inspector Ji Ye proposed opening the Dukang reservoir for military colonies; harvests of hundreds of thousands of piculs yearly made the northern frontier self-sufficient.

sentences.zh: 又於河內置懷義等屯，以給河南之費。

translations.literal: Again at Henei he established the Huaiyi and other colonies to supply the expenses of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He also established the Huaiyi colonies in Henei to feed the armies south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 自是稍止轉輸之勞。

translations.literal: From this the labor of long transport was somewhat stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Long supply trains grew less necessary.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊申，周改元保定。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on wushen, Zhou changed the era name to Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, first month, on wushen, Northern Zhou changed the era name to Baoding.

sentences.zh: 以大塚宰護為都督中外諸軍事；

translations.literal: Grand minister of state Hu was made Commander of All Forces Inside and Outside;
translations.idiomatic: Grand minister of state Yuwen Hu was made commander of all forces inside and outside;

sentences.zh: 令五府總於天官，事無鉅細，皆先斷後聞。

translations.literal: the five bureaus were gathered under the celestial office; affairs great and small were all decided first and reported after.
translations.idiomatic: the five ministries were folded under the celestial office; great and small matters alike were decided first and reported afterward.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，大赦。

translations.literal: On gengxu, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 周主祀圜丘。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler sacrificed at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou ruler sacrificed at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，齊主祀圜丘；

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Qi ruler sacrificed at the Round Mound;
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the Qi ruler sacrificed at the Round Mound;

sentences.zh: 壬子，示帝於太廟。

translations.literal: on renzi, presented the emperor in the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: on renzi, presented the imperial tablets in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 周主祀方丘；

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler sacrificed at the Square Mound;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou ruler sacrificed at the Square Mound;

sentences.zh: 甲寅，祀感生帝於南郊；

translations.literal: on jiayin, sacrificed to the Life-Giving Emperor at the southern suburb;
translations.idiomatic: on jiayin, sacrificed to the Life-Giving Emperor at the southern suburb;

sentences.zh: 乙卯，祭太社。

translations.literal: on yimao, offered to the Great Altar of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: on yimao, offered to the Great Altar of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 齊主使王琳出合肥，召募傖楚，更圖進取。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler sent Wang Lin out from Hefei to recruit Sogdian and Chu levies and plot advance again.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler sent Wang Lin from Hefei to raise Sogdian and Chu troops and plan a new offensive.

sentences.zh: 合州刺史裴景徽，琳兄鈱之婿也，請以私屬為鄉導。

translations.literal: Hezhou Inspector Pei Jinghui, son-in-law of Lin's elder brother Qin, asked to use his private followers as guides.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhou inspector Pei Jinghui, who had married Lin's brother's daughter, offered his household retainers as guides.

sentences.zh: 齊主使琳與行台左丞盧潛將兵赴之，琳沉吟不決。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler ordered Lin and Left Assistant Director of the Mobile Headquarters Lu Qian to lead troops thither; Lin hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler ordered Lin and mobile-headquarters left assistant director Lu Qian to march; Lin hesitated.

sentences.zh: 景徽恐事洩，挺身奔齊。

translations.literal: Jinghui feared the affair would leak and threw himself into flight to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure, Jinghui fled to Qi alone.

sentences.zh: 齊主以琳為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史，鎮壽陽。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler made Lin Flying Cavalry Grand General, Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, and Yangzhou Inspector, garrisoning Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler made Lin flying-cavalry grand general, palace attendant of the third rank, and inspector of Yangzhou, stationed at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 己巳，周主享太廟，班太祖所述六官之法。

translations.literal: On jisi, the Zhou ruler offered in the imperial temple and promulgated the law of the six offices as stated by the Founding Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, the Zhou ruler offered in the ancestral temple and promulgated the six-office system laid down by the founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 辛未，周湘州城主殷亮降，湘州平。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Zhou Xiangzhou city chief Yin Liang surrendered; Xiangzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Zhou's Xiangzhou garrison commander Yin Liang surrendered; Xiangzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 侯瑱與賀若敦相持日久，瑱不能制，乃借船送敦等渡江。

translations.literal: Hou Tian and He Ruo Dun faced each other long; Tian could not control him and therefore borrowed boats to send Dun and others across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Tian and He Ruo Dun had faced each other for months without advantage; Tian borrowed boats to ferry Dun's army across the river.

sentences.zh: 敦慮其詐，不許，報云：「湘州我地，為爾侵逼；

translations.literal: Dun feared deceit and would not permit it; he replied, saying, "Xiangzhou is our land—you have encroached upon it;
translations.idiomatic: Dun suspected a trap and refused; he answered: "Xiangzhou is ours—you invaded it;

sentences.zh: 必須我歸，可去我百里之外。

translations.literal: you must let me return; you may withdraw a hundred li from me.
translations.idiomatic: I will withdraw only if you pull back a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 」瑱留船江岸，引兵去之。

translations.literal: " Tian left boats on the riverbank and led his troops away.
translations.idiomatic: " Tian left the boats on the bank and marched off.

sentences.zh: 敦乃自拔北歸，軍士病死者什五六。

translations.literal: Dun then broke camp himself and returned north; sick and dead soldiers were five or six in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Dun then broke north; five or six soldiers in ten died of sickness on the march.

sentences.zh: 武陵、天門、南平、義陽、河東、宜都郡悉平。

translations.literal: Wuling, Tianmen, Nanping, Yiyang, Hedong, and Yidu commanderies were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wuling, Tianmen, Nanping, Yiyang, Hedong, and Yidu were all recovered.

sentences.zh: 晉公護以敦失地無功，除名為民。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu, because Dun lost land without achievement, struck his name and made him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu stripped Dun of rank for losing ground without gain.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲午，周主朝日於東郊。

translations.literal: Second month, on jiawu, the Zhou ruler attended the sun at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, on jiawu, the Zhou ruler worshipped the sun at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 周人以小司徒韋孝寬嘗立勳於玉壁，乃置勳州於玉壁，以孝寬為刺史。

translations.literal: The people of Zhou, because Lesser Minister of Education Wei Xiaokuan had once won merit at Yubi, therefore established Xunzhou at Yubi and made Xiaokuan inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wei Xiaokuan had won fame at Yubi, Zhou created Xunzhou there and made him inspector.

sentences.zh: 孝寬有恩信，善用間諜，或齊人受孝寬金貨，遙通書疏，故齊之動靜，周人皆先知之。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan had kindness and trustworthiness and used spies well; some Qi men took Xiaokuan's gold and goods and sent letters from afar—therefore Qi's movements Zhou men always knew first.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan ruled with kindness and excelled at espionage; Qi men took his gold and sent word from afar—Zhou always knew Qi's moves first.

sentences.zh: 有主帥許盆，以所戍城降齊，孝寬遣諜取之，俄斬首而還。

translations.literal: A garrison commander Xu Pen surrendered the city he held to Qi; Xiaokuan sent spies to take him and soon returned with his head severed.
translations.idiomatic: When garrison commander Xu Pen surrendered his post to Qi, Xiaokuan's agents seized him and were back with his head in no time.

sentences.zh: 離石以南，生胡數為抄掠，而居於齊境，不可誅討。

translations.literal: South of Lishi, raw Hu often raided, yet dwelt within Qi territory and could not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: South of Lishi, tribal Hu raided often but lived within Qi's border and could not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 孝寬欲築城於險要以制之，乃發河西役徒十萬，甲士百人，遣開府儀同三司姚岳監築之。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan wished to build a city at a strategic pass to control them; he therefore mobilized one hundred thousand corvée laborers from west of the river and one hundred armored soldiers, and sent Palace Attendant of the Third Rank Yao Yue to oversee the building.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan meant to build a fortress at a choke point; he drafted a hundred thousand laborers from west of the river and a hundred armored men, with palace attendant Yao Yue to supervise.

sentences.zh: 岳以兵少，懼不改前。

translations.literal: Yue, because troops were few, feared things would not change from before.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, with so few troops, feared the raiders would not change their ways.

sentences.zh: 孝寬曰：「計此城十日可畢。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan said, "I calculate this city can be finished in ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan said, "This fort can be finished in ten days.

sentences.zh: 城距晉州四百餘里，吾一日創手，二日敵境始知。

translations.literal: The city is more than four hundred li from Jinyang; on one day we begin, on the second day the enemy border first knows.
translations.idiomatic: It lies four hundred li from Jinyang; we break ground on day one, and the border learns on day two.

sentences.zh: 設使晉州徵兵，三日方集，謀議之間，自稽三日，計其軍行，二日不到。

translations.literal: Suppose Jinyang mobilizes troops—they gather only on the third day; in counsel and debate three days pass of themselves; counting their march, two days they do not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose Jinyang mobilizes: three days to assemble, three more in council, two on the road—they still will not arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 我之隍防，足得辦矣。

translations.literal: Our walls and defenses will be enough to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Our walls will stand before they come.

sentences.zh: 」乃令築之。

translations.literal: " He then ordered it built.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered construction to begin.

sentences.zh: 齊人果至境上，疑有大軍，停留不進。

translations.literal: Qi men indeed reached the border, suspected a great army, halted and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Qi troops reached the border, suspected a great army, and halted.

sentences.zh: 其夜，孝寬使汾水以南傍介山、稷山諸村縱火。

translations.literal: That night Xiaokuan had villages south of the Fen River near Jieshan and Jishan set fires.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xiaokuan had villages south of the Fen, near Jieshan and Jishan, set fires.

sentences.zh: 齊人以為軍營，收兵自固。

translations.literal: Qi men took them for army camps and gathered troops to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Qi took the fires for encampments and drew their men in.

sentences.zh: 岳卒城而還。

translations.literal: Yue finished the city and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yue finished the fort and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙卯，太尉零陵壯肅公侯瑱卒。

translations.literal: Third month, on yimao, Grand Marshal the stalwart and solemn Duke of Lingling Hou Tian died.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, on yimao, grand marshal Hou Tian, Duke of Lingling, died.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，周改八丁兵為十二丁兵，率歲一月役。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Zhou changed eight-ding soldiers to twelve-ding soldiers, on average one month of service per year.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Zhou changed the levy from eight men per ding to twelve, with one month of service per year on average.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on the bingzi new moon, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, at the bingzi new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 周以少傅尉遲綱為大司空。

translations.literal: Zhou made Junior Tutor Yuchi Gang Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou made junior tutor Yuchi Gang grand minister of works.

sentences.zh: 丙午，周封愍帝子康為紀國公，皇子贇為魯國公。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Zhou enfeoffed the son of Emperor Min, Kang, as Duke of the State of Ji, and the prince Yun as Duke of the State of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Zhou enfeoffed Emperor Min's son Kang as duke of Ji and Prince Yun as duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 贇，李後之子也。

translations.literal: Yun was son of Empress Li.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was a son of Empress Li.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙酉，周主使御正殷不害來聘。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on yiyou, the Zhou ruler sent Director of Documents Yin Buhai on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, on yiyou, the Zhou ruler sent director of documents Yin Buhai on a friendly mission.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，周更鑄錢，文曰「布泉」，一當五，與五銖並行。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Zhou recoined money; the inscription read "Buquan"; one counted as five and circulated with the five-zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, Zhou recoined money inscribed "Buquan," valued at five old coins and circulated alongside the five-zhu.

sentences.zh: 己酉，周追封皇伯父顥為邵國公，以晉公護之子會為嗣；

translations.literal: On jiyou, Zhou posthumously enfeoffed the emperor's father's elder brother Hao as Duke of the State of Shao, with Duke of Jin Hu's son Hui as heir;
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Zhou posthumously enfeoffed the emperor's grand-uncle Hao as duke of Shao, with Yuwen Hu's son Hui as heir;

sentences.zh: 顥弟連為杞國公，以章武公導之子亮為嗣；

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Lian as Duke of the State of Qi, with Duke Zhangwu Dao's son Liang as heir;
translations.idiomatic: Hao's brother Lian as duke of Qi, with Zhangwu duke Dao's son Liang as heir;

sentences.zh: 連弟洛生為莒國公，以護之子至為嗣；

translations.literal: Lian's younger brother Luosheng as Duke of the State of Ju, with Hu's son Zhi as heir;
translations.idiomatic: Lian's brother Luosheng as duke of Ju, with Hu's son Zhi as heir;

sentences.zh: 追封太祖之子武邑公震為宋公，以世宗之子實為嗣。

translations.literal: posthumously enfeoffed the Founding Ancestor's son Duke Zhen of Wuyi as Duke of Song, with Emperor Shizong's son Shi as heir.
translations.idiomatic: and posthumously raised the founding ancestor's son Zhen of Wuyi to duke of Song, with Shizong's son Shi as heir.

sentences.zh: 齊主之誅楊、燕也。

translations.literal: When the Qi ruler executed Yang and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi ruler had executed Yang Yin and his faction.

sentences.zh: 許以長廣王湛為太弟；

translations.literal: He had promised Prince Zhan of Changgung the title Grand Younger Brother;
translations.idiomatic: He had promised Prince Zhan of Changgung the title of grand younger brother;

sentences.zh: 既而立太子百年，湛心不平。

translations.literal: yet afterward he established crown prince Bainian—Zhan's heart was not level.
translations.idiomatic: yet then made young Bainian crown prince—and Zhan's heart turned sour.

sentences.zh: 帝在晉陽，湛居守於鄴。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Jinyang; Zhan remained to guard Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Jinyang; Zhan held Ye.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍高元海，高祖之從孫也。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Gao Yuanhai was a younger cousin's grandson of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Gao Yuanhai was a great-grandson of Gaozu on a collateral line.

sentences.zh: 留典機密。

translations.literal: He was left to manage secrets.
translations.idiomatic: He was left in charge of confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝以領軍代人庫狄伏連為幽州刺史，以斛律光之弟羨為領軍，以分湛權。

translations.literal: The emperor made Army Director Kudi Fulian of Daiyou Inspector of Youzhou, and Hulü Guang's younger brother Xian Army Director, to divide Zhan's power.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent army director Kudi Fulian to Youzhou as inspector and made Hulü Guang's brother Xian army director, to split Zhan's power.

sentences.zh: 湛留伏連，不聽羨視事。

translations.literal: Zhan detained Fulian and would not let Xian take up his post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan kept Fulian at Ye and blocked Xian from taking office.

sentences.zh: 先是，濟南閔悼王常在鄴，望氣者以鄴中有天子氣。

translations.literal: Earlier the Lamented Prince of Jinan had long been at Ye; men who read the qi said Ye held the emperor's breath.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed prince of Jinan had long been kept at Ye; geomancers said the city breathed with imperial qi.

sentences.zh: 平秦王歸彥恐濟南王復立，為己不利，勸帝除之。

translations.literal: Prince Guiyan of Pingqin feared the Prince of Jinan would be restored, to his own harm, and urged the emperor to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guiyan of Pingqin, fearing Jinan's restoration would undo him, urged the emperor to kill him.

sentences.zh: 帝乃使歸彥至鄴，征濟南王如晉陽。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent Guiyan to Ye to summon the Prince of Jinan to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Guiyan to Ye to bring the prince of Jinan to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 湛內不自安，問計於高元海。

translations.literal: Zhan was inwardly ill at ease and asked Gao Yuanhai for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in his heart, Zhan asked Gao Yuanhai for counsel.

sentences.zh: 元海曰：「皇太后萬福，至尊孝友異常，殿下不須異慮。

translations.literal: Yuanhai said, "The empress dowager enjoys ten thousand blessings; the sovereign is unusually filial and brotherly—Your Highness need not other worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai said, "The empress dowager is well; the emperor is dutiful beyond measure—you need not fret.

sentences.zh: 」湛曰：「此豈我推誠之意邪！

translations.literal: " Zhan said, "Is this the sort of counsel I asked for in good faith!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhan said, "That is not the honest counsel I asked for!

sentences.zh: 」元海乞還省，一夜思之，湛即留元海於後堂。

translations.literal: " Yuanhai begged to return to his office and think one night; Zhan at once kept Yuanhai in the rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanhai asked leave to withdraw and think overnight; Zhan kept him in the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 元海達旦不眠，唯繞床徐步。

translations.literal: Yuanhai until dawn did not sleep, only pacing slowly around the bed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai did not sleep until dawn, pacing slowly around the couch.

sentences.zh: 夜漏未盡，湛遽出，曰：「神算如何？

translations.literal: Before the night watch ended, Zhan hurried out and said, "What is the divine reckoning?
translations.idiomatic: Before the night watch ended, Zhan burst in: "What is your verdict?

sentences.zh: 」元海曰：「有三策，恐不堪用耳。

translations.literal: " Yuanhai said, "There are three plans—I fear they may not be usable.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanhai said, "There are three plans—though you may find them hard to take.

sentences.zh: 請殿下如梁孝王故事，從數騎入晉陽，先見太后求哀，後見主上，請去兵權，以死為限，不干朝政，必保泰山之安。

translations.literal: I ask Your Highness to follow the story of Prince Xiao of Liang: with a few horsemen enter Jinyang, first see the empress dowager and beg mercy, then see the sovereign and ask to lay down military power, with death as the limit, not meddling in court affairs—you will surely keep Mount Tai's peace.
translations.idiomatic: Ride to Jinyang with a few horsemen as Prince Xiao of Liang did: beg the empress dowager first, then the emperor; surrender your command and swear never to meddle in court—you will live secure as Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 此上策也。

translations.literal: This is the upper plan.
translations.idiomatic: That is the best course.

sentences.zh: 不然，當具表雲，威權太盛，恐取謗眾口，請青、齊二州刺史，沉靖自居，必不招物議。

translations.literal: Otherwise you should submit a memorial saying your authority is too great and you fear slander from many mouths, and request the inspectorships of Qing and Qi, dwelling in quiet composure—you will surely not draw public criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Or memorialize that your power alarms the court and ask for Qing and Qi provinces—live quietly and men will not talk.

sentences.zh: 此中策也。

translations.literal: This is the middle plan.
translations.idiomatic: That is the middle course.

sentences.zh: 」更問下策。

translations.literal: " He again asked for the lower plan.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhan pressed for the third.

sentences.zh: 曰：「發言即恐族誅。

translations.literal: He said, "To speak is to fear execution of the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhai said, "To speak it is to risk the death of your house.

sentences.zh: 」固逼之，元海曰：「濟南世嫡，主上假太后令而奪之。

translations.literal: " Pressed firmly, Yuanhai said, "Jinan is the legitimate heir; the sovereign borrowed the empress dowager's order to seize it from him.
translations.idiomatic: " When Zhan pressed him, Yuanhai said, "Jinan is the rightful heir; the throne was taken from him on a forged order.

sentences.zh: 今集文武，示以征濟南之敕，執斛律豐樂，斬高歸彥，尊立濟南，號令天下，以順討逆，此萬世一時也。

translations.literal: Now gather civil and military, show the edict summoning Jinan, seize Hulü Fengle, behead Gao Guiyan, install Jinan in honor, command the realm, and with obedience punish rebellion—this is the chance of ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Summon civil and military, produce the order that called Jinan north, seize Hulü Fengle, kill Gao Guiyan, set Jinan on the throne, and march under the banner of righteousness—such a chance comes once in an age.

sentences.zh: 」湛大悅。

translations.literal: " Zhan was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhan was delighted.

sentences.zh: 然性怯，狐疑未能用，使術士鄭道謙等卜之，皆曰：「不利舉事，靜則吉。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was timid; hesitating and doubting, he could not use it; he had diviners Zheng Daoqian and others cast lots—all said, "Unfavorable to raise affairs; if still, auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was timid; he could not act. Diviners Zheng Daoqian and others cast lots—all said, "Do not move; stillness brings fortune.

sentences.zh: 」有林慮令潘子密，曉占候，潛謂湛曰：「宮車當晏駕，殿下為天下主。

translations.literal: " There was Linlu magistrate Pan Zimi, skilled in observing signs, who secretly told Zhan, "The imperial carriage will soon halt; Your Highness will be lord of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: " Linlu magistrate Pan Zimi, skilled in omens, whispered to Zhan: "The emperor's death is near—you will rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 」湛拘之於內以候之。

translations.literal: Zhan detained him inside to wait and see.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan held him within the palace to watch events unfold.

sentences.zh: 又令巫覡卜之，多云「不須舉兵，自有大慶」。

translations.literal: He also had shamans divine; most said, "No need to raise troops—great fortune will come of itself."
translations.idiomatic: He had shamans divine as well; most answered, "Do not take up arms—great fortune will come unbidden."

sentences.zh: 湛乃奉詔，令數百騎送濟南王至晉陽。

translations.literal: Zhan then obeyed the edict and sent several hundred horsemen to escort the Prince of Jinan to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan obeyed the edict and sent several hundred horsemen to escort the Prince of Jinan to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝使人鴆之，濟南王不從，乃扼殺之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the emperor sent men to poison him; the Prince of Jinan refused, and they strangled him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor sent poison; the Prince of Jinan would not drink it, and they strangled him.

sentences.zh: 帝尋亦悔之。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor regretted it too.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor regretted it as well.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day jiaxu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, on the first day jiaxu, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 丙子，齊以彭城王浟為太保，長樂王尉粲為太尉。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Qi made Prince You of Pengcheng Grand Guardian and Prince Can of Changle Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Northern Qi made Prince You of Pengcheng grand guardian and Prince Can of Changle grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 齊肅宗出畋，有兔驚馬，墜地絕肋。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong of Qi went hunting; a hare startled his horse and he fell, breaking his ribs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong of Qi went hunting; a hare startled his horse and he fell, his ribs snapped.

sentences.zh: 婁太后視疾，問濟南所在者三，齊主不對。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Lou visited his sickbed and three times asked where the Prince of Jinan was; the Qi ruler did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Lou came to his sickbed and thrice asked where the Prince of Jinan was; the Qi ruler would not answer.

sentences.zh: 太后怒曰：「殺之邪？

translations.literal: The empress dowager raged: "You killed him?
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager raged: "You killed him?

sentences.zh: 不用吾言，死其宜矣！

translations.literal: You would not heed my words—death was fitting!"
translations.idiomatic: You would not heed me—death was fitting!"

sentences.zh: 」遂去，不顧。

translations.literal: She left and would not look back.
translations.idiomatic: She turned away and would not look back.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲辰，詔以嗣子沖眇，可遣尚書右僕射趙郡王睿諭旨，征長廣王湛統茲大寶。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiachen, an edict held that the heir was young and faint; Right Vice Director Prince Rui of Zhao might convey the intent and summon Prince Zhan of Changguang to hold the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, on jiachen, an edict declared the heir too young and ordered Right Vice Director Prince Rui of Zhao to summon Prince Zhan of Changguang to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又與湛書曰：「百年無罪，汝可以樂處置之，勿效前人也。

translations.literal: He also wrote Zhan: "Bainian is innocent—you may place him at Lechu. Do not imitate your predecessors."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Zhan: "Bainian is innocent—set him at Lechu in comfort. Do not do as those before you."

sentences.zh: 」是日，殂於晉陽宮。

translations.literal: That day he died at Jinyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That day he died at Jinyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 臨終，言恨不見太后山陵。

translations.literal: At the end he said he regretted not seeing the empress dowager's tomb mound completed.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he said he grieved that he would not see the empress dowager's tomb completed.

sentences.zh: 顏之推論曰：孝昭天性至孝，而不知忌諱，乃至於此，良由不學之所為也。

translations.literal: Yan Zhitui remarked: Xiaozhao was filial by nature yet ignorant of taboo, even to this—truly the work of one who had not studied.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhitui wrote: Xiaozhao was filial by nature yet blind to taboo, even to this—what comes of a life without learning.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王睿先使黃門侍郎王松年馳至鄴，宣肅宗遺命。

translations.literal: Prince Rui of Zhao first sent Palace Attendant Wang Songnian galloping to Ye to proclaim Xiaozong's final command.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui of Zhao first sent palace attendant Wang Songnian galloping to Ye with Xiaozong's last command.

sentences.zh: 湛猶疑其詐，使所親先詣殯所，發而視之。

translations.literal: Zhan still suspected deceit and sent a close man first to the mourning hall to open the coffin and look.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan still suspected a ruse and sent a trusted man to the mourning hall to open the coffin and look.

sentences.zh: 使者覆命，湛喜，馳赴晉陽，使河南王孝瑜先入宮，改易禁衛。

translations.literal: When the envoy reported back, Zhan rejoiced, raced to Jinyang, and sent Prince Xiaoyu of Henan into the palace first to change the guards.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy returned; Zhan rejoiced, raced to Jinyang, and sent Prince Xiaoyu of Henan ahead to replace the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，世祖即皇帝位於南宮，大赦，改元太寧。

translations.literal: On guichou, Emperor Shizu took the throne at the Southern Palace, proclaimed amnesty, and changed the era to Taining.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Emperor Shizu took the throne at the Southern Palace, proclaimed amnesty, and changed the era to Taining.

sentences.zh: 周人許歸安成王頊，使司會上士京兆杜杲來聘。

translations.literal: The Zhou people agreed to return Prince Xu of Ancheng and sent Chief Clerk of the Department of State Affairs Du Gao of Jingzhao on a mission.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou agreed to return Prince Xu of Ancheng and sent chief clerk Du Gao of Jingzhao on an embassy.

sentences.zh: 上悅，即遣使報之，並賂以黔中地及魯山郡。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, at once sent envoys in reply, and ceded Qianzhong and Lushan commandery as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, sent envoys at once in reply, and ceded Qianzhong and Lushan commandery as gifts.

sentences.zh: 齊以彭城王浟為太師、錄尚書事，平秦王歸彥為太傅，尉粲為太保，平陽王淹為太宰，博陵王濟為太尉，段韶為大司馬，豐州刺史婁睿為司空，趙郡王睿為尚書令，任城王湝為尚書左僕射，并州刺史斛律光為右僕射。

translations.literal: Qi made Prince You of Pengcheng Grand Preceptor and Recorder of the Secretariat; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin Grand Tutor; Can Grand Guardian; Prince Yan of Pingyang Grand Mentor; Prince Ji of Boling Grand Commandant; Duan Shao Grand Marshal; Lou Rui of Fengzhou Minister of Works; Prince Rui of Zhao Director of the Secretariat; Prince Cheng of Rencheng Left Vice Director; Hu Lv Guang of Bingzhou Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi made Prince You of Pengcheng grand preceptor and recorder of the Secretariat; Prince Guiyan of Pingqin grand tutor; Can grand guardian; Prince Yan of Pingyang grand mentor; Prince Ji of Boling grand commandant; Duan Shao grand marshal; Lou Rui of Fengzhou minister of works; Prince Rui of Zhao director of the Secretariat; Prince Cheng of Rencheng left vice director; Hu Lv Guang of Bingzhou right vice director.

sentences.zh: 婁睿，韶之兄子也。

translations.literal: Lou Rui was Duan Shao's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Rui was nephew to Duan Shao's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 立太子百年為樂陵王。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Bainian was made Prince of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Bainian was made prince of Leling.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，周主畋於岐陽；

translations.literal: On dingsi, the Zhou ruler hunted at Qiyang;
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, the Zhou ruler hunted at Qiyang;

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬午，還長安。

translations.literal: in the twelfth month, on renwu, he returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: twelfth month, on renwu, he returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 太子中庶子餘姚虞荔、御史中丞孔奐，以國用不足，奏立煮海鹽賦及榷酤之科，詔從之。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Attendant Yu Li of Yuyao and Imperial Censor Kong Huan, because state revenue was insufficient, memorialized to establish sea-salt boiling levies and monopoly on wine sales; the edict followed.
translations.idiomatic: Crown prince attendant Yu Li of Yuyao and imperial censor Kong Huan, finding the treasury bare, memorialized for sea-salt levies and a wine monopoly; the court assented.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖以帝女豐安公主妻留異之子貞臣，征異為南徐州刺史，異遷延不就。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gaozu had married the Princess of Feng'an to Liu Yi's son Zhenchen and summoned Yi as Inspector of South Xuzhou; Yi delayed and would not come.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gaozu had married Princess Feng'an to Liu Yi's son Zhenchen and summoned Yi as inspector of South Xuzhou; Yi delayed and would not come.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，復以異為縉州刺史，領東海太守。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, he again made Yi Inspector of Jinzhou and concurrent Administrator of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, he again made Yi inspector of Jinzhou and concurrent administrator of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 異屢遣其長史王澌入朝，澌每言朝廷虛弱。

translations.literal: Yi repeatedly sent his chief clerk Wang Si to court; Si always said the court was weak.
translations.idiomatic: Yi repeatedly sent chief clerk Wang Si to court; Si always said the throne was weak.

sentences.zh: 異信之，雖外示臣節，恆懷兩端，與王琳自鄱陽信安嶺潛通使往來。

translations.literal: Yi believed him. Though outwardly he showed subject's duty, he always harbored two minds and secretly exchanged envoys with Wang Lin by way of Xin'an Ridge in Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi believed him. Outwardly loyal, inwardly he wavered, and exchanged secret envoys with Wang Lin across Xin'an Ridge in Poyang.

sentences.zh: 琳敗，上遣左衛將軍沈恪代異，實以兵襲之。

translations.literal: When Lin was defeated, the emperor sent Left Guard General Shen Ke to replace Yi—in truth to strike him with troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin fell, the emperor sent left guard general Shen Ke to replace Yi—in truth to strike him with troops.

sentences.zh: 異出軍下淮以拒恪，恪與戰而敗，退還錢塘。

translations.literal: Yi led troops out to Xiahuai to resist Ke; Ke fought and was defeated, and withdrew to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi marched to Xiahuai to meet Ke; Ke was beaten and withdrew to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 異復上表遜謝。

translations.literal: Yi again submitted a memorial of humble apology.
translations.idiomatic: Yi again submitted a humble apology.

sentences.zh: 時眾軍方事湘、郢，乃降詔書慰諭，且羈縻之。

translations.literal: At that time the armies were engaged at Xiang and Ying, so an edict of comfort was sent and he was held on loose reins.
translations.idiomatic: The armies were busy at Xiang and Ying, so the court sent comforting words and held him on loose reins.

sentences.zh: 異知朝廷終將討己，乃以兵戍下淮及建德以備江路。

translations.literal: Yi knew the court would eventually punish him, so he garrisoned Xiahuai and Jiande to guard the river route.
translations.idiomatic: Yi knew the court would come for him at last and garrisoned Xiahuai and Jiande to guard the river road.

sentences.zh: 丙午，詔司空、南徐州刺史侯安都討之。

translations.literal: On bingwu, an edict ordered Minister of Works and Inspector of South Xuzhou Hou An'du to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the court ordered minister of works and inspector of South Xuzhou Hou An'du against him.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙亥，齊主至鄴；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yihai, the Qi ruler reached Ye;
translations.idiomatic: Spring, first month, on yihai, the Qi ruler reached Ye;

sentences.zh: 辛巳，祀南郊；

translations.literal: on xinsi, he sacrificed at the Southern Altar;
translations.idiomatic: on xinsi, he sacrificed at the southern altar;

sentences.zh: 壬午，享太廟；

translations.literal: on renwu, he offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple;
translations.idiomatic: on renwu, he offered at the imperial temple;

sentences.zh: 丙戌，立妃胡氏為皇后，子緯為皇太子。

translations.literal: on bingxu, he made Consort Hu empress and his son Wei crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: on bingxu, he made Consort Hu empress and his son Wei crown prince.

sentences.zh: 後，魏兗州刺史安定胡延之之子也。

translations.literal: The empress was daughter of Hu Yanzhi of Anding, Inspector of Yanzhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was daughter of Hu Yanzhi of Anding, Wei's inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊子，大赦。

translations.literal: On wuzi, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以馮翊王潤為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On jihai, Prince Run of Fengyi was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Prince Run of Fengyi was made left vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 周涼景公賀蘭祥卒。

translations.literal: Duke Jing of Liang, Helan Xiang of Zhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jing of Liang, Helan Xiang of Northern Zhou, died.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，周人鑿河渠於蒲州，龍首渠於同州。

translations.literal: On renyin, the Zhou people dug a canal at Puzhou and the Longshou Canal at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Northern Zhou dug a canal at Puzhou and the Longshou Canal at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁未，周以安成王頊為柱國大將軍，遣杜果送之南歸。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Zhou made Prince Xu of Ancheng Grand General of the Pillars and sent Du Guo to escort him south.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Northern Zhou made Prince Xu of Ancheng grand general of the pillars and sent Du Guo to escort him south.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，上祀南郊，以胡公配天；

translations.literal: On xinhai, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar, with Duke Hu as companion to Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the emperor sacrificed at the southern altar, with Duke Hu as companion to Heaven;

sentences.zh: 二月，辛酉，祀北郊。

translations.literal: in the second month, on xinyou, he sacrificed at the Northern Altar.
translations.idiomatic: second month, on xinyou, he sacrificed at the northern altar.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丁未，齊以太宰、平陽王淹為青州刺史，太傅、平秦王歸彥為太宰、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on dingwei, Qi made Grand Mentor Prince Yan of Pingyang Inspector of Qingzhou and Grand Tutor Prince Guiyan of Pingqin Grand Mentor and Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary month, on dingwei, Northern Qi made grand mentor Prince Yan of Pingyang inspector of Qingzhou and grand tutor Prince Guiyan of Pingqin grand mentor and inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 歸彥為肅宗所厚，恃勢驕盈，陵侮貴戚。

translations.literal: Guiyan had been favored by Xiaozong; relying on power he grew arrogant and insulted the nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan had been favored by Xiaozong; swollen with power he insulted the great houses.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，侍中、開府儀同三司高元海、御史中丞畢義雲、黃門郎高乾和數言其短，且云：「歸彥威權震主，必為禍亂。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Palace Attendant Gao Yuanhai, Imperial Censor Bi Yiyun, and Yellow Gate Gentleman Gao Qianhe repeatedly spoke of his faults, saying, "Guiyan's authority shakes the ruler—he will bring calamity."
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu took the throne, palace attendant Gao Yuanhai, imperial censor Bi Yiyun, and yellow gate gentleman Gao Qianhe denounced him again and again: "Guiyan's power eclipses the throne—he will bring ruin."

sentences.zh: 」帝亦尋其反覆之跡，漸忌之。

translations.literal: The emperor also traced his shifting loyalties and grew to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor traced his shifting loyalties and grew to fear him.

sentences.zh: 伺歸彥還家，召魏收於帝前作詔草，除歸彥冀州，使乾和繕寫。

translations.literal: When Guiyan returned home, he summoned Wei Shou before him to draft the edict removing Guiyan to Jizhou and had Qianhe fair-copy it.
translations.idiomatic: When Guiyan went home, he summoned Wei Shou to draft the edict moving Guiyan to Jizhou and had Qianhe fair-copy it.

sentences.zh: 晝日，仍敕門司不聽歸彥輒入宮。

translations.literal: That same day he ordered the gate office not to let Guiyan enter the palace at will.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he ordered the gate office to bar Guiyan from the palace.

sentences.zh: 時歸彥縱酒為樂，經宿不知。

translations.literal: Guiyan was then drinking deep for pleasure and knew nothing until the night had passed.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan was drinking deep and knew nothing until dawn.

sentences.zh: 至明，欲參，至門知之，大驚而退。

translations.literal: At dawn he wished to attend court; reaching the gate he learned of it, was greatly alarmed, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he came to court; at the gate he learned the truth, started back in terror, and fled.

sentences.zh: 及通名謝，敕令早發，別賜錢帛等物甚厚，又敕督將悉送至清陽宮。

translations.literal: When he announced his name to take leave, the order commanded early departure and separately bestowed money and silk in great measure; he also ordered escort officers to see him all the way to Qingyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When he took formal leave, the order bade him depart at once, heaped gifts upon him, and sent escorts to Qingyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 拜辭而退，莫敢與語，唯趙郡王睿與之久語，時無聞者。

translations.literal: He bowed and withdrew; none dared speak with him—only Prince Rui of Zhao talked long with him, and for the moment none overheard.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed and withdrew; none dared speak with him save Prince Rui of Zhao, who talked long—and none overheard.

sentences.zh: 帝之為長廣王也，清都和士開發善握槊、彈琵琶有寵，闢為開府行參軍，及即位，累遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When the emperor had been Prince of Changguang, He Shikai of Qinghe, skilled at backgammon and the pipa, was favored; he was made acting staff officer of the prince's mansion, and after enthronement was promoted to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had been Prince of Changguang, He Shikai of Qinghe, master of backgammon and the pipa, won favor; he rose to attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 高元海、畢義雲、高乾和皆疾之，將言其事。

translations.literal: Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, and Gao Qianhe all resented him and were about to report the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuanhai, Bi Yiyun, and Gao Qianhe hated him and were about to expose him.

sentences.zh: 士開乃奏元海等交結朋黨，欲擅威福。

translations.literal: Shikai then memorialized that Yuanhai and the rest formed factions and sought to monopolize authority and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai memorialized that Yuanhai and the rest had formed a faction to seize power and favor.

sentences.zh: 乾和由是被疏。

translations.literal: Qianhe was thereby estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Qianhe was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 義雲納賂於士開，得為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Yiyun bribed Shikai and was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyun bribed Shikai and won appointment as inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝征江州刺史周迪出鎮湓城，又征其子入朝。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Inspector of Jiangzhou Zhou Di to take post at Pencheng and also summoned his son to court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Jiangzhou inspector Zhou Di to Pencheng and his son to court.

sentences.zh: 迪趑且顧望，並不至。

translations.literal: Di hesitated and looked about; neither came.
translations.idiomatic: Di hesitated and looked about; neither came.

sentences.zh: 其餘南江酋帥，私署令長，多不受召，朝廷未暇致討，但羈縻之。

translations.literal: The other chieftains of the southern rivers privately appointed magistrates and mostly would not answer summons; the court had no leisure to punish them and only held them on loose reins.
translations.idiomatic: Other southern chieftains appointed their own magistrates and ignored summons; the court had no leisure to punish them and only held them loosely.

sentences.zh: 豫章太守周敷獨先入朝，進號安西將軍，給鼓吹一部，賜又女妓、金帛，令還豫章。

translations.literal: Administrator of Yuzhang Zhou Fu alone came to court first; he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West, given a set of martial pipes, female entertainers and gold and silk besides, and ordered back to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhang administrator Zhou Fu alone came to court first; he was made general who pacifies the west, given martial pipes, courtesans, gold, and silk, and sent back to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 迪以敷素出己下，深不平之，乃陰與留異相結，遣其弟方興將兵襲敷；

translations.literal: Di, because Fu had always ranked below him, was deeply resentful; he secretly joined Liu Yi and sent his brother Fangxing with troops to raid Fu;
translations.idiomatic: Di resented Fu, who had always ranked below him; he secretly allied with Liu Yi and sent his brother Fangxing to raid him;

sentences.zh: 敷與戰，破之。

translations.literal: Fu fought and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu fought and routed him.

sentences.zh: 又遣其兄子伏甲船中，詐為賈人，欲襲湓城。

translations.literal: He again sent his elder brother's son with hidden armor in ships, feigning to be merchants, intending to strike Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his nephew with armed men hidden in merchant ships to strike Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 未發，事覺，尋陽太守監江州事晉陵華皎遣兵逆擊之，盡獲其船仗。

translations.literal: Before they set out the plot was discovered; Xunyang Administrator and acting overseer of Jiangzhou Hua Jiao of Jinling sent troops to intercept and seized all their ships and arms.
translations.idiomatic: Before they sailed the plot was discovered; Xunyang administrator Hua Jiao of Jinling intercepted them and seized ships and arms.

sentences.zh: 上以閩州刺史陳寶應之父為光祿大夫，子女皆受封爵，命宗正編入屬籍。

translations.literal: The emperor made the father of Chen Baoying, Inspector of Minzhou, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; sons and daughters all received ranks, and the Director of the Imperial Clan was ordered to enter them in the lineage register.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Minzhou inspector Chen Baoying's father grand master for splendid happiness, ennobled his children, and ordered the director of the imperial clan to enter them in the lineage register.

sentences.zh: 而寶應以留異女為妻，陰與異合。

translations.literal: But Baoying had taken Liu Yi's daughter as wife and secretly joined with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: But Baoying had married Liu Yi's daughter and secretly aided him.

sentences.zh: 虞荔弟寄，流寓閩中，荔思之成疾，上為荔征之，寶應留不遣。

translations.literal: Yu Li's younger brother Ji was stranded in Min; Li pined until ill, and the emperor summoned Ji for Li's sake, but Baoying detained him and would not send him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Li's brother Ji was stranded in Min; Li sickened with longing, and though the emperor summoned Ji for his sake, Baoying would not release him.

sentences.zh: 寄嘗從容諷以逆順，寶應輒引它語以亂之。

translations.literal: Ji once gently admonished him with the logic of loyalty and rebellion; Baoying always turned the talk elsewhere to confuse the point.
translations.idiomatic: Ji once gently spoke of loyalty and rebellion; Baoying always turned the talk aside.

sentences.zh: 寶應嘗使人讀《漢書》，臥而聽之，至蒯通說韓信曰：「相君之背，貴不可言。

translations.literal: Baoying once had someone read the Book of Han while he lay listening; when it came to Kuai Tong saying to Han Xin, "Turning your back on the lord—nobility beyond words,"
translations.idiomatic: Baoying once had the Book of Han read to him as he lay listening; at Kuai Tong telling Han Xin, "Turn your back on your lord—glory beyond words,"

sentences.zh: 」蹶然起坐，曰：「可謂智士！

translations.literal: he started up and said, "Truly a wise man!"
translations.idiomatic: he started up and cried, "Now there was a wise man!"

sentences.zh: 」寄曰：「通一說殺三士，何足稱智！

translations.literal: Ji said, "Tong with one speech killed three men—how is that called wisdom!"
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Tong's one speech killed three men—what wisdom is that!"

sentences.zh: 豈若班彪《王命》，識所歸乎！

translations.literal: How does that compare with Ban Biao's 'Kingly Mandate,' which knows where to turn?"
translations.idiomatic: Better Ban Biao's 'Kingly Mandate,' which knows where loyalty lies!"

sentences.zh: 寄知寶應不可諫，恐禍及己，乃著居士服，居東山寺，陽稱足疾。

translations.literal: Ji knew Baoying could not be remonstrated with and feared harm would reach him; he put on layman's robes, dwelt at East Hill Temple, and pretended foot ailment.
translations.idiomatic: Ji knew Baoying would not listen and feared for his life; he took lay robes, dwelt at East Hill Temple, and feigned lameness.

sentences.zh: 寶應使人燒其屋，寄安臥不動。

translations.literal: Baoying sent men to burn his dwelling; Ji lay still and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying sent men to burn his hut; Ji lay still.

sentences.zh: 親近將扶之出，寄曰：「吾命有所懸，避將安往！

translations.literal: Those close were about to help him out; Ji said, "My fate is suspended—where would fleeing take me!"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants would have dragged him out; Ji said, "My fate hangs elsewhere—where would I flee!"

sentences.zh: 」縱火者自救之。

translations.literal: Those who had set the fire themselves saved him.
translations.idiomatic: The men who set the fire themselves pulled him out.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，齊以任城王湝為司徒。

translations.literal: On yimao, Qi made Prince Cheng of Rencheng Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Northern Qi made Prince Cheng of Rencheng minister of education.

sentences.zh: 齊揚州剌史行台王琳數欲南侵，尚書盧潛以為時事未可。

translations.literal: Wang Lin, Inspector of Yangzhou and head of the Eastern Office, repeatedly wished to invade south; Director of the Secretariat Lu Qian held the times not yet ripe.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou inspector Wang Lin, head of the eastern office, repeatedly wished to strike south; secretariat director Lu Qian held the moment unripe.

sentences.zh: 上遣移書壽陽，欲與齊和親。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a letter to Shouyang seeking peace and kinship with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a letter to Shouyang seeking peace with Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 潛以其書奏齊朝，仍上啟且請息兵。

translations.literal: Qian presented the letter to the Qi court and also memorialized asking to cease arms.
translations.idiomatic: Qian presented the letter to the Qi court and memorialized for a halt to arms.

sentences.zh: 齊主許之，遣散騎常侍崔瞻來聘，且歸南康愍王曇朗之喪。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler agreed, sent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Cui Zhan on a mission, and also returned the coffin of Prince Min of Nankang, Tanlang.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler agreed, sent attendant Cui Zhan on an embassy, and returned the coffin of Prince Min of Nankang, Tanlang.

sentences.zh: 琳由是與潛有隙，更相表列。

translations.literal: Lin thereby bore a grudge against Qian, and they repeatedly denounced each other in memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and Qian became enemies and denounced each other in memorial after memorial.

sentences.zh: 齊主征琳赴鄴，以潛為揚州刺史，領行台尚書。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler summoned Lin to Ye and made Qian Inspector of Yangzhou and concurrent Director of the Eastern Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler summoned Lin to Ye and made Qian inspector of Yangzhou and head of the eastern office.

sentences.zh: 瞻，凌之子也。

translations.literal: Zhan was son of Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was Ling's son.

sentences.zh: 梁末喪亂，鐵錢不行，民間私用鵝眼錢。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang's turmoil iron coin would not circulate; among the people goose-eye coin was used in secret.
translations.idiomatic: At Liang's fall iron coin would not pass; the people used goose-eye cash in secret.

sentences.zh: 甲子，改鑄五銖錢，一當鵝眼之十。

translations.literal: On jiazi, they recast five-zhu coin, one equal to ten goose-eye.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi they recast five-zhu cash, each worth ten goose-eye.

sentences.zh: 後梁主安於儉素，不好酒色，雖多猜忌，而撫將士有恩。

translations.literal: The ruler of Later Liang was content with plain living, disliked wine and women, and though much given to suspicion, treated officers with grace.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Liang ruler lived plainly, shunned wine and women, and though suspicious treated his officers with grace.

sentences.zh: 以封疆褊隘，邑居殘毀，干戈日用，鬱鬱不得志，疽發背而殂；

translations.literal: Because his domain was narrow and settlements ruined, war came daily; depressed and without fulfillment, a carbuncle rose on his back and he died;
translations.idiomatic: His realm was narrow, his towns in ruins, war daily at hand; he brooded without hope until a carbuncle on his back killed him;

sentences.zh: 葬平陵，謚曰宣皇帝，廟號中宗。

translations.literal: he was buried at Pingling, posthumous title Emperor Xuan, temple name Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: he was buried at Pingling, posthumous title Emperor Xuan, temple name Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 太子巋即皇帝位，改元天保；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Kui took the throne and changed the era to Tianbao;
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Kui took the throne and changed the era to Tianbao;

sentences.zh: 尊龔太后為太皇太后，王后曰皇太后，母曹貴嬪為皇太妃。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Gong was honored as grand empress dowager; the queen was styled empress dowager; the mother, Noble Consort Cao, was made grand imperial consort.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Gong was honored as grand empress dowager; the queen became empress dowager; Noble Consort Cao, the emperor's mother, became grand imperial consort.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙子，安成王頊至建康，詔以為中書監、中衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingzi, Prince Xu of Ancheng reached Jiankang; an edict made him Director of the Secretariat and Central Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, on bingzi, Prince Xu of Ancheng reached Jiankang and was made director of the Secretariat and central guard general.

sentences.zh: 上謂杜杲曰：「家弟今蒙禮遣，實周朝之惠；

translations.literal: The emperor said to Du Gao, "My younger brother now receives courteous return—truly Zhou's grace;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Du Gao, "My brother returns with honor—truly Zhou's grace;

sentences.zh: 然魯山不返，亦恐未能及此。

translations.literal: yet had Lushan not been returned, I fear this might not have been reached."
translations.idiomatic: yet without Lushan's return, I doubt we would have seen this day."

sentences.zh: 」杲對曰：「安成，長安—布衣耳，而陳之介弟也，其價豈止一城而已哉！

translations.literal: Gao answered, "Ancheng in Chang'an was but a commoner, yet he is Chen's younger brother by the same mother—his worth is surely more than one city!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao answered, "In Chang'an Prince Xu was a commoner—but he is Chen's own brother. His worth is more than one city!"

sentences.zh: 本朝敦睦九族，恕己及物，上遵太祖遣旨，下思繼好之義，是以遣之南歸。

translations.literal: "Our court cherishes the nine clans, extends forgiveness from oneself to things, above follows the founding emperor's last command, below considers the meaning of continuing friendship—therefore he was sent south."
translations.idiomatic: "Our court honors kinship, forgives as we would be forgiven, obeys the founder's charge, and seeks lasting peace—therefore he was sent south."

sentences.zh: 今乃雲以導常之土易骨肉之親，非使臣之所敢聞也。

translations.literal: "Now to say common soil is exchanged for flesh-and-blood kin—that is not what this envoy dares hear."
translations.idiomatic: "To trade common earth for blood kin—that is not for this envoy's ears."

sentences.zh: 」上甚慚，曰：「前言戲之耳。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply ashamed and said, "My earlier words were only in jest."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flushed and said, "I spoke in jest."

sentences.zh: 」待杲之禮有加焉。

translations.literal: His treatment of Gao grew still more courteous.
translations.idiomatic: His courtesy toward Gao only increased.

sentences.zh: 頊妃柳氏及子叔寶猶在穰城，上復遣毛喜如周請之，周人皆歸之。

translations.literal: Xu's consort Lady Liu and son Shubao were still at Rang; the emperor again sent Mao Xi to Zhou to request them, and the Zhou people returned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's consort Lady Liu and son Shubao remained at Rang; the emperor sent Mao Xi to Zhou to ask for them, and Zhou returned them.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以安右將軍吳明徹為江州刺史，督高州刺史黃法□、豫章太守周敷共討周迪。

translations.literal: On dingchou, General of the Right Guard Wu Mingche was made Inspector of Jiangzhou to oversee Inspector Huang Fa□ of Gaozhou and Administrator Zhou Fu of Yuzhang in joint campaign against Zhou Di.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, general of the right guard Wu Mingche was made inspector of Jiangzhou to oversee Gaozhou inspector Huang Fa□ and Yuzhang administrator Zhou Fu against Zhou Di.

sentences.zh: 甲申，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiashen, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 留異始謂台軍必自錢塘上，既而侯安都步由諸暨出永康，異大驚，奔桃枝嶺，於巖口豎柵以拒之。

translations.literal: Liu Yi had first thought the imperial army would come up from Qiantang; instead Hou An'du marched by foot from Zhuji out through Yongkang. Yi was greatly alarmed, fled to Taozhi Ridge, and set palisades at the cliff mouth to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi expected the imperial army from Qiantang; instead Hou An'du marched from Zhuji through Yongkang. Yi fled to Taozhi Ridge and raised palisades at the cliff mouth.

sentences.zh: 安都為流矢所中，血流至踝，乘轝指麾，容止不變。

translations.literal: An'du was struck by a stray arrow; blood ran to his ankles, yet riding in a litter he directed the battle, his bearing unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: A stray arrow struck An'du; blood ran to his ankles, yet from his litter he commanded, his bearing unchanged.

sentences.zh: 因其山勢，迮而為堰。

translations.literal: Using the mountain's slope, he narrowed it into a dam.
translations.idiomatic: He used the slope to pen the water into a dam.

sentences.zh: 會潦水漲滿，安都引船入堰，起樓艦與異城等，發拍碎其樓堞。

translations.literal: When floodwaters rose full, An'du brought ships into the dam, raised tower-ships level with Yi's walls, and launched rams that shattered the battlements.
translations.idiomatic: When the floods rose, An'du brought ships into the dam, raised tower-ships level with Yi's walls, and smashed his battlements with rams.

sentences.zh: 異與其子忠臣脫身奔晉安，依陳寶應。

translations.literal: Yi and his son Zhongchen escaped to Jin'an and relied on Chen Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and his son Zhongchen fled to Jin'an and threw themselves on Chen Baoying.

sentences.zh: 安都虜其妻及餘子，盡收鎧仗而還。

translations.literal: An'du captured his wife and remaining sons, gathered all armor and weapons, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: An'du took his wife and remaining sons, seized arms and armor, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 異黨向文政據新安，上以貞毅將軍程文季為新安太守，帥精甲三百徑往攻之。

translations.literal: Yi's partisan Xiang Wenzheng held Xin'an; the emperor made General of Firm Resolution Cheng Wenji Administrator of Xin'an and led three hundred picked armored men straight to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's partisan Xiang Wenzheng held Xin'an; the emperor sent general of firm resolution Cheng Wenji as administrator with three hundred picked men straight against him.

sentences.zh: 文政戰敗，遂降。

translations.literal: Wenzheng was defeated in battle and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzheng was beaten and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 文季，靈洗之子也。

translations.literal: Wenji was son of Cheng Lingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji was Cheng Lingxi's son.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛丑，齊武明婁太后殂。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinchou, Empress Dowager Lou Wuming of Qi died.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, on xinchou, Empress Dowager Lou Wuming of Northern Qi died.

sentences.zh: 齊主不改服，緋袍如故。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler did not change dress; his scarlet robe remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler did not change dress; he still wore scarlet.

sentences.zh: 未幾，登三台，置酒作樂，宮女進白袍，帝投諸台下。

translations.literal: Before long he ascended the Three Terraces, set out wine and made music; palace women brought white robes and the emperor threw them below the terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he climbed the Three Terraces for wine and music; palace women brought white robes and he hurled them from the terrace.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍和士開請止樂，帝怒，撾之。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant He Shikai asked that the music cease; the emperor raged and beat him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant He Shikai begged him to stop; the emperor raged and beat him.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，帝遣使來聘。

translations.literal: On yisi, the emperor sent envoys on a mission.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, the Chen emperor sent envoys on an embassy.

sentences.zh: 齊青州上言河水清，齊主遣使祭之，改元河清。

translations.literal: Qingzhou in Qi reported the river waters clear; the Qi ruler sent envoys to sacrifice and changed the era to Heqing.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou reported clear river water; the Qi ruler sacrificed and changed the era to Heqing.

sentences.zh: 先是，周之群臣受封爵者皆未給租賦。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhou ministers who had received enfeoffment had not been granted rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: Until then, Northern Zhou nobles had received no rent from their fiefs.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，始詔柱國等貴臣邑戶，聽寄食它縣。

translations.literal: On guihai, an edict first granted fief households to pillar-state and other great ministers, allowing them to draw sustenance from other counties.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai an edict first granted fief households to pillar-state and other great lords, allowing sustenance drawn from other counties.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚午，周大赦。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on gengwu, Zhou proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, on gengwu, Northern Zhou proclaimed general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 己丑，齊以右僕射斛律光為尚書令。

translations.literal: On jichou, Qi made Right Vice Director Hu Lv Guang Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Northern Qi made right vice director Hu Lv Guang director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，周以柱國楊忠為大司空。

translations.literal: On renchen, Zhou made Pillar-State Yang Zhong Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Northern Zhou made pillar-state Yang Zhong grand minister of works.

sentences.zh: 六月，巳亥，以柱國蜀國公尉遲迥為大司馬。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jihai, Pillar-State Duke Yuchi Jiong of Shu was made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, on jihai, pillar-state Duke Yuchi Jiong of Shu was made grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己丑，納太子妃王氏，金紫光祿大夫周之女也。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jichou, the crown prince's consort Lady Wang was received—daughter of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, on jichou, the crown prince took Lady Wang, daughter of grand master of splendid happiness Zhou.

sentences.zh: 齊平秦王歸彥至冀州，內不自安，欲待齊主如晉陽，乘虛入鄴。

translations.literal: Prince Guiyan of Pingqin reached Jizhou, ill at ease within, and wished to wait until the Qi ruler went to Jinyang, then seize Ye while it was empty.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guiyan of Pingqin reached Jizhou uneasy within, planning to wait until the ruler went to Jinyang and then seize empty Ye.

sentences.zh: 其郎中令呂思禮告之。

translations.literal: His director of the palace bureau Lü Sil reported him.
translations.idiomatic: His palace bureau director Lü Sil reported him.

sentences.zh: 詔大司馬段韶、司空婁睿討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Marshal Duan Shao and Minister of Works Lou Rui to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered grand marshal Duan Shao and minister of works Lou Rui against him.

sentences.zh: 歸彥於南境置私驛，聞大軍將至，即閉城拒守。

translations.literal: Guiyan had set private post stations on the southern border; hearing the great army was coming, he at once shut the city and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan had private post stations on the southern border; hearing the army approach, he shut the gates.

sentences.zh: 長史宇文仲鸞等不從，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Yuwen Zhongluan and others would not follow; he killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Yuwen Zhongluan and others refused; he killed them all.

sentences.zh: 歸彥自稱大丞相，有眾四萬。

translations.literal: Guiyan styled himself Grand Chancellor and had forty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan styled himself grand chancellor and mustered forty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 齊主以都官尚書封子繪，冀州人，祖父世為本州刺史，得人心，使乘傳至信都，巡城，諭以禍福，吏民降者相繼，城中動靜，小大皆知之。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler, because Minister of Justice Feng Zihui was a man of Jizhou whose grandfather and father for generations had been inspectors of that province and won men's hearts, sent him by post-cart to Xindu to tour the walls and speak of fortune and ruin; officials and people surrendered in succession, and great and small within the city knew every movement.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler sent minister of justice Feng Zihui—whose family had held Jizhou for generations and won men's hearts—by post-cart to Xindu to tour the walls and speak of fortune and ruin; the city surrendered in waves, and every movement within was known.

sentences.zh: 歸彥登城大呼云：「孝昭皇帝初崩，六軍百萬，悉在臣手，投身向鄴，奉迎陛下。

translations.literal: Guiyan mounted the wall and shouted, "When Emperor Xiaozhao first died, the six armies—a million men—were all in my hand. I threw myself toward Ye and welcomed Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan mounted the wall and shouted, "When Xiaozhao died, a million men of the six armies were in my hand. I raced to Ye and raised you to the throne.

sentences.zh: 當時不反，今日豈反邪！

translations.literal: I did not rebel then—how would I rebel today!
translations.idiomatic: I did not rebel then—would I rebel now!
